title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate EEG Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) can characterize functional brain alterations in multiple sclerosis (MS), but many EEG features vary with age. We therefore examined resting-state EEG associations with MS using age-adjusted models while explicitly accounting for the severe age imbalance in the available dataset. Resting-state 128-channel EEG data from the BrainLat dataset were analyzed. Demographic files included 32 patients with MS and 32 healthy controls (HC); global-feature models included 29 patients with MS and 32 HC, and channel-level sample sizes varied by feature. Diagnosis and age were entered in linear models. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied separately to five global spectral/aperiodic tests, 16 global microstate tests, and the 128 channel-wise tests within each feature. Within-MS continuous age regression and exploratory age-stratified ANOVA were evaluated with the same family definitions. After correction, diagnosis coefficients were significant for global bandwidth (β = 1.928, q = 0.0287), global aperiodic offset (β = 1.816, q = 3.29 × 10⁻⁷), and offset at all 128 channels (β range = 1.52-2.41; q range = 3.56 × 10⁻⁸ to 7.43 × 10⁻⁵). Global central frequency, exponent, PSD, and all 16 microstate measures did not survive FDR correction. No within-MS continuous-age or age-stratified result survived FDR correction. Aperiodic offset showed the strongest diagnosis association under the specified age-adjusted model. However, the MS and HC age ranges did not overlap (21-55 vs 56-83 years), so the diagnosis coefficient depends on extrapolation and cannot establish an MS-specific effect. The findings are exploratory and require age-matched replication with detailed clinical, vigilance, site, sex, and MRI characterization.

title: Targeting the Immune-Neurovascular Interface to Ameliorate Pericyte Dysfunction with a Multifunctional Peptide-Drug Conjugate Nanoprodrug for Multiple Sclerosis Therapy.
abstract: Pericyte dysfunction triggers blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and subsequent aberrant immune infiltration in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet targeted interventions remain lacking. Here, we engineered a dual-functional fusion peptide (VLC) for pericyte targeting and therapeutic intervention and subsequently conjugated it with luteolin to construct a peptide-drug conjugate (PDC)-based ROS-responsive nanoprodrug (VLC@Lut-NPs). This system significantly suppressed MMP-9 overactivation and mitigated neuroinflammation. To optimize the pharmacokinetic profile of the PDC nanotherapeutic, we adopted subcutaneous administration, achieving a prolonged circulation half-life and enhancing brain drug accumulation (AUCbrain) by 2.65-fold compared with intravenous injection. In two MS models, VLC@Lut-NPs restored pericyte homeostasis, reinforced BBB integrity, attenuated aberrant peripheral immune infiltration, and ultimately promoted myelin repair and regeneration. Notably, a once-every-other-day subcutaneous regimen outperformed daily intravenous administration. By bridging peripheral immunity and the neurovascular unit, this work identifies pericytes as a central regulatory node and establishes a pericyte-targeted PDC nanoplatform for durable MS treatment, highlighting its translational potential as a complementary strategy to conventional immunomodulatory approaches.

title: Multimodal effects of CD40L blockade in multiple sclerosis: Insights from preclinical and clinical studies.
abstract: Costimulatory signaling is essential for T-cell activation, tolerance, and immune homeostasis. Dysregulation of these pathways contributes to autoimmune diseases, including multiple sclerosis. Therapeutic targeting of costimulatory molecules, particularly the CD40-CD40L axis, has demonstrated clinical success in several autoimmune conditions, including multiple sclerosis. This review integrates mechanistic insights from experimental models with clinical data to examine the effects of CD40L blockade across diverse immune and central nervous system-resident cell populations. Preclinical models highlight the complex interplay between immune cells and central nervous system-resident cells beyond costimulatory signaling alone. Clinical mechanistic studies support CD40L blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy for multiple sclerosis.

title: Spinal cord lesions and visually assessed focal cord atrophy are associated with long-term disability outcomes in multiple sclerosis: a real-world retrospective cohort study.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of spinal cord lesions and cord atrophy for long-term disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains unclear in real-world cohorts. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 223 patients with relapse-onset MS. The earliest pre-treatment spinal MRI was scored for lesion characteristics, gadolinium enhancement, and focal cord atrophy, assessed in 172 lesion-positive patients. Outcomes, referenced to one-year EDSS, included EDSS worsening (conventional magnitude criteria), incident EDSS ≥ 3 at last assessment, clinician-recorded progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA), and conversion to secondary progressive MS (SPMS). Firth-penalised logistic and Cox models were adjusted for baseline EDSS, age at diagnosis, and sex (logistic models also for disease duration). RESULTS: Cord lesions were present in 172 patients (77.1%), and all outcomes were more frequent in this group (EDSS worsening 39.5% vs 13.7%, incident EDSS ≥ 3 31.5% vs 6.1%, PIRA 22.7% vs 5.9%, SPMS conversion 15.1% vs 3.9%; all p ≤ 0.04). Lesion presence was associated with EDSS worsening (OR 3.56, 95% CI 1.55-9.21), incident EDSS ≥ 3 (5.31, 1.62-22.74), and PIRA (4.09, 1.17-20.43). Among lesion-positive patients, focal atrophy was associated with EDSS worsening (2.72, 1.22-6.23), incident EDSS ≥ 3 (5.59, 1.96-17.18), PIRA (3.66, 1.41-9.67), and SPMS conversion (HR 4.07, 1.69-9.82), with a graded pattern across lesion/atrophy status. Topographical features showed no consistent association. CONCLUSION: Spinal cord involvement was associated with every disability outcome examined, and among lesion-positive patients, visually assessed focal atrophy distinguished those with the worst course. The qualitative exposure, unconfirmed endpoints, and retrospective design make these findings hypothesis-generating; they support standardised prospective spinal imaging rather than individual prognostication.

title: Assessment of development and implementation of collaborative practice agreements in an integrated health system specialty pharmacy.
journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
abstract: PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to describe the development and implementation of collaborative pharmacy practice agreements (CPPAs) in an integrated health-system specialty pharmacy (HSSP) using the RE-AIM (reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance) framework. METHODS: An observational, cross-sectional, mixed-methods convergent study design was used to assess CPPA implementation in infectious diseases (ID), multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunology (MSN), hemostasis, hepatology, neurology-movement disorders, and cystic fibrosis (CF) clinics. For the qualitative phase, focus groups and semistructured interviews were conducted with HSSP leadership, clinical pharmacists, and physician champions. For the quantitative phase, data were collected retrospectively from the health system's electronic health record for the 6 months post CPPA implementation. RESULTS: A total of 14 clinical pharmacists participated in focus groups across 6 different specialty clinics. Post-CPPA implementation themes highlighted improved patient care, including shorter time to treatment and better monitoring; high compatibility with existing clinic workflow; high acceptability by clinic staff; and the need for resources to support implementation. Pharmacists ordered 2,388 medications over the 6-month post-CPPA implementation time frame. Within clinics that implemented laboratory ordering to support medication management (the MSN, adult hepatology, and ID clinics), pharmacists ordered 764 laboratory tests. CONCLUSIONS: Within an integrated HSSP, implementing CPPAs was well received by clinic staff, with notable perceptions of reductions in staff workload and improved patient care. HSSPs considering CPPAs should consider resources beyond clinical pharmacists alone to support development and implementation requirements.

title: Recent advances in multiple sclerosis neurorehabilitation.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Advances in multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis and treatment have altered disease trajectories, yet many people with MS (pwMS) continue to experience complex symptom burden, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life (QoL). This review summarizes recent developments in neurorehabilitation, focusing on screening and assessment, intervention delivery, and outcome or impact evaluation across symptoms and disability domains. RECENT FINDINGS: Research evidence supports routine, multidimensional screening that goes beyond assessing symptom severity to capture functional limitations, participation restrictions, and social determinants of health (SDoH). Digital technologies, including wearables, remote monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted assessments, offer opportunities for more ecologically valid and accessible evaluation, although usability, digital exclusion, and implementation issues remain. Neurorehabilitation is increasingly viewed as a treatment that should begin early in the disease course rather than being reserved for advanced disability. Exercise interventions, cognitive rehabilitation, psychological therapies, vocational rehabilitation, and integrated multidisciplinary approaches demonstrate benefits across physical, cognitive, emotional, fatigue, and QoL outcomes. Telerehabilitation and technology-supported interventions, including virtual reality, exergaming, and neuromodulation, show promise in improving access and outcomes, but more research is needed. To sustain long-term neurorehabilitation benefits, teaching self-management strategies and brain-health behaviours may be beneficial. SUMMARY: Neurorehabilitation is a core component of comprehensive MS care, complementing pharmacological treatment. Evidence favours early, personalized, function-focused interventions delivered through flexible, tiered, and multidisciplinary models. Research gaps include implementation of screening pathways, optimization of person-to-treatment matching and dosing, integration of SDoH, development of meaningful patient-centred outcomes, evaluation of cost-effectiveness, and improved equity of access to rehabilitation services and research across diverse populations.

title: Structural Social Connection, Biological Ageing, and Neurodegenerative Disease Burden: A Global Ecological Analysis of Household Size and Modelled Dementia Incidence Estimates.
abstract: Poor social connection and ageing-related biological processes are recognised contributors to Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. However, cross-national evidence linking structural indicators of social connection with dementia and broader neurological dis-ease burden remains limited. This ecological study examined country-level associations be-tween average household size and modelled neurological disease incidence estimates. Country- and territory-level data from up to 204 settings were analysed. Average household size was the primary exposure, and model-derived, age-standardised incidence-rate estimates for Alzheimer's disease and other dementias were the primary outcome. Par-kinson's disease, motor neuron disease, multiple sclerosis, idiopathic epilepsy, headache dis-orders, and total neurological disorders were examined as comparative secondary outcomes. The Henneberg Index, life expectancy at age 60, GDP per capita, and urban living were in-cluded as contextual covariates. Analyses included Pearson and Spearman correlations, par-tial correlations, principal component analysis, and multivariable linear regression. Household size was strongly and inversely associated with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias incidence estimates (Pearson r=-.841, p<.001). The association remained after adjustment for the included covariates (β=-.569, p<.001). Significant inverse adjusted associations were also observed for Parkinson's disease, motor neuron disease, and total neurological disorders, whereas patterns differed for other neurological outcomes. Principal component analysis identified a single ageing-development dimension explaining 72.1% of the variance, with household size loading inversely against life expectancy at age 60, econom-ic affluence, urban living, and the Henneberg Index. Smaller average household size was associated with higher modelled incidence estimates for dementia and selected neurodegenerative diseases at the country level. These findings should be interpreted as ecological associations rather than evidence of individual-level causation and suggest that household structure is embedded within broader demograph-ic, socioeconomic, and ageing-related processes.

title: Disease-modifying interventions in psychiatry.
journal: The Australian and New Zealand journal of psychiatry
abstract: Disease-modifying interventions do not just treat the symptoms of the disease but target the underlying disease process and natural course. The construct of disease-modifying treatments has transformed the care of disorders, like rheumatoid arthritis and multiple sclerosis, by shifting the focus to preventing end-organ damage rather than offering symptomatic treatment. As mental illness may have a chronic and progressive course, there is a need to consider whether any of our interventions may be disease-modifying. We, therefore, conducted a search using databases, including MEDLINE, EMBASE and PsycINFO, to identify peer-reviewed papers and grey literature related to the research question: 'Which psychiatric treatments are disease-modifying?' Disease-modifying properties were largely operationalised around end-organ changes, including structural brain changes evident on neuroimaging and cognition, and were reported for conventional psychotropics, as well as for novel pharmaceuticals and non-pharmacological interventions. Lithium and electroconvulsive therapy showed the greatest evidence as disease-modifying interventions. However, to establish this and identify potential other disease-modifying treatments, there needs to be a shift in the focus of psychiatric clinical trials to include primary outcomes that reflect disease progression and not just acute symptom burden. The potential disease-modifying properties of lithium and electroconvulsive therapy should spur the prioritisation of treatment higher up the algorithm, as well as the commencement of disease-modifying therapy as early as possible in the illness course to prevent adverse outcomes.

title: Gain-of-Function Variants in PLAAT4 and Spinal Predominant Demyelinating Leukodystrophy.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Leukoencephalopathies are clinically and etiologically heterogeneous disorders, and establishing a specific diagnosis remains challenging. Patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and brain white matter hyperintensities (WMH) may be misdiagnosed as having multiple sclerosis, potentially exposing them to unnecessary immunosuppressive therapy. OBJECTIVE: To define the clinical, radiological, and genetic features of spinal predominant demyelinating leukodystrophy with leg spasticity (SPDMLS). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This case series involved participants from 4 tertiary referral hospitals within the China Alliance for Rare Diseases during the period July 2019 to August 2025. The study design integrated clinical evaluations and whole-exome sequencing (WES), as well as targeted plasma lipidomics correlated with SPATAX-EUROSPA disability stages. Variant pathogenicity was evaluated using an oligodendrocyte-specific knock-in mouse model. Participants were patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and central nervous system (CNS) WMH and available family members, including presymptomatic carriers. EXPOSURES: WES, genetic characterization, testing. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Identification of disease-associated gene and characterization of clinical, radiological, and genetic features of SPDMLS. RESULTS: Twenty-six individuals from 11 unrelated families were included; 4 patients underwent longitudinal follow-up for up to 5 years. Recurrent heterozygous PLAAT4 (phospholipase A and acyltransferase 4) variants (p.I14T and p.A96V) were associated with a novel autosomal dominant leukoencephalopathy, named SPDMLS. Age at onset was 11 to 51 years (median [IQR], 22 [15-29] years), with patients predominantly developing spastic paraplegia. Symbol Digit Modalities Test scores ranged from 11 to 70 in 6 available patients. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated slow progression with heterogeneous brain WMH and a stereotyped pattern of symmetric, long-segment "girdle-like" spinal cord WMH accompanied by atrophy. Somatosensory- and motor-evoked potentials indicated dysfunction of the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts, respectively. In presymptomatic carriers, spinal cord signal alterations preceded brain involvement. An oligodendrocyte-specific knock-in mouse model provided in vivo functional evidence supporting a role of PLAAT4 gain-of-function in driving demyelination, informing SPDMLS pathogenesis. Patient plasma lipidomics suggested accumulation of arachidonic acid-related lipids correlating with disability stage. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that PLAAT4 variants delineated SPDMLS, a clinically distinct leukodystrophy that should be considered in patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and CNS WMH. Arachidonic acid-related lipids represent a candidate biomarker for disease progression.

title: Perivascular Diffusivity and Periventricular Susceptibility Changes in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Combined DTI-ALPS and QSM Study.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
abstract: BACKGROUND: Progressive periventricular damage in multiple sclerosis (MS) has been linked to impaired perivascular clearance and to susceptibility changes attributed to iron deposition and myelin loss. Their relationship is unclear. PURPOSE/HYPOTHESIS: To compare diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) and periventricular quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) between relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) patients and healthy controls; and to evaluate their correlation and relationships with clinical disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale, EDSS). STUDY TYPE: Retrospective case-control study. POPULATION/SUBJECTS: Thirty one patients with RRMS (mean age, 34.6 ± 8.4 years) and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age, 34.2 ± 8.1 years). FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 1.5 T; Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and multi-echo gradient-echo (GRE) sequences. ASSESSMENT: DTI-ALPS index and periventricular QSM values were measured from manually placed bilateral regions of interest (ROIs). Standardized Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI)-space coordinates were used for DTI-ALPS analysis, and QSM ROIs in periventricular normal-appearing white matter were reviewed by a neuroradiologist. Disability was assessed using the EDSS. STATISTICAL TESTS: Groups were compared using independent-samples t-tests and Cohen's d. Correlations were assessed using Pearson's r, with Spearman's rho as a sensitivity analysis (p < 0.05, two-tailed). RESULTS: DTI-ALPS was lower in MS patients than controls (1.27 ± 0.22 vs. 1.45 ± 0.22; d = 0.828), whereas periventricular QSM was higher (-15.35 ± 4.92 vs. -21.70 ± 6.40 ppb; d = 1.116). A strong negative correlation between the two biomarkers was observed across all subjects (r = -0.738). Both measures correlated with EDSS (DTI-ALPS r = -0.509; QSM r = 0.501) and differed between EDSS subgroups (EDSS > 2.0 vs. ≤ 2.0: DTI-ALPS 1.160 vs. 1.364; QSM -12.33 vs. -17.83 ppb). DATA CONCLUSION: Reduced DTI-ALPS and higher periventricular QSM-derived susceptibility were each moderately associated with disability in RRMS. The negative DTI-ALPS-QSM correlation in both groups indicates an association between perivascular diffusivity, a putative marker of glymphatic function, and periventricular QSM-derived susceptibility; causality cannot be established from this cross-sectional design. STAGE OF TECHNICAL EFFICACY: 2.

title: Multiple sclerosis burden: global versus MENA region (1990 to 2023), with mortality projections to 2050: A pairwise GBD analysis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) burden is rising in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), a region long considered low-prevalence. This study compared MS mortality, incidence, and prevalence between MENA and global populations from 1990 to 2023. GBD 2023 age-standardized mortality (ASMR), incidence (ASIR), and prevalence (ASPR) rates for 21 MENA countries and globally were analyzed with joinpoint regression, comparing average annual percentage changes (AAPC) with z-tests adjusted for MENA's inclusion in the global estimate. Death counts were decomposed into population growth, ageing, and ASMR change, and country trends were stratified by income group and subregion. Global ASMR declined from 0.23 to 0.21 per 100,000 (AAPC -0.28%), whereas MENA ASMR rose from 0.14 to 0.24 (AAPC +1.67%; p < 0.001 versus global), although its GBD uncertainty interval included zero. Global deaths rose 97% through population growth (+52%) and ageing (+42%) despite a 9% ASMR decline; MENA deaths rose 376% through population growth (+99%), ageing (+40%), and rising ASMR (+71%). MENA incidence (AAPC +0.33% vs -0.03%) and prevalence (+0.54% vs +0.26%) outpaced global rates, and female mortality in MENA outpaced male mortality (+2.22% vs +0.97%). Country trends did not differ by income group or subregion. By 2050, mortality was projected to fall 26.3% globally against 10.5% in MENA. Age-standardized MS incidence and prevalence are rising in MENA, more so in females, while global trends remain largely stable. Rising deaths in both populations largely reflect population growth and ageing. MS registries, disease-modifying therapy access, and neurorehabilitation investment are needed.

title: The role of comorbidities in comprehensive healthcare utilization among people with multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Many people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) live with comorbid conditions, which may contribute to more complex healthcare needs. While there have been several studies on their associations with increased hospitalizations and emergency visits, there has been limited investigation into other aspects of care (e.g., imaging) or composite indices have been used rather than individual conditions. To determine If comorbidities in PwMS are associated with utilization of a wider range of healthcare services and which specific comorbid conditions are linked to those services. Participants (n = 185) were PwMS who completed a series of questionnaires about their comorbidities and healthcare utilization over the prior 12 months as part of a larger study. Regression models were used to evaluate the relationships between healthcare utilization and specific comorbidities, controlling for age, gender, race, education, and annual income. PwMS with a comorbidity had higher utilization of several services, including more healthcare provider visits (p < 0.001), particularly with primary care (p = .041) and mental health providers (p = .003), unique providers seen (p < 0.001), active medications (p < .001), MRIs (p = .008), X-rays (p = .031), inpatient hospital stays (p = .038), and elective surgeries (p = .035). Several comorbidities, including anxiety, sleep apnea, autoimmune thyroid disease, and irritable bowel syndrome, were most frequently associated with increased service use. These findings expand upon the previous literature, demonstrating that comorbidities are associated with greater utilization of a wide range of services and the complex needs of PwMS living with multiple chronic conditions.

title: Mechanisms and therapeutic strategies for central and peripheral remyelination.
abstract: Myelin sheaths are produced by myelinating glia and provide metabolic support to neuronal axons while accelerating electrical signal conduction. Myelinating glia, which include oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) and Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), have distinct developmental origins and biological characteristics that profoundly influence their capacity for myelin regeneration following demyelinating insults. In various demyelinating diseases, loss of myelin and myelinating glia resulting from autoimmune disorders, inflammation, or genetic defects causes neurological dysfunction. Beyond removing disease-causing factors, inducing and accelerating remyelination represents a critical therapeutic goal for demyelinating diseases. In this review, we first summarize and compare molecular mechanisms underlying CNS and PNS remyelination, including extracellular signaling pathways, transcriptional regulation, and intercellular communication. We then highlight current treatments and ongoing clinical trials for common demyelination disorders, including neonatal white matter injury, multiple sclerosis, and inherited peripheral neuropathies.

title: Plasma microRNA dysregulation in treatment-naïve primary progressive multiple sclerosis: an exploratory case-control study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) is a disabling phenotype marked by gradual neurological worsening from disease onset and limited biomarker availability. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have become candidate regulators and biomarkers in neuroinflammatory disorders. PPMS-specific plasma miRNA data, particularly from treatment-naïve patients, remain limited. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this exploratory case-control study, plasma samples from 20 newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve patients with PPMS and 25 healthy controls with broadly comparable age and sex distributions were assayed for 84 neurologically relevant miRNAs using high-throughput real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction on the BioMark HD platform. Expression data were normalized using the global mean method. Differential expression was evaluated in a candidate-discovery framework, and experimentally supported target genes and pathways were examined through in silico enrichment analyses. Twenty-six miRNAs exhibited nominal between-group differences, of which 24 remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction at q < 0.05. The largest decreases included let-7b-5p, miR-26b-5p, miR-20a-5p, and miR-15b-5p, whereas miR-191-5p, miR-320a-3p, miR-146a-5p, and miR-342-3p were among the most elevated candidates. Integrated analyses associated the biologically prioritized target set with miRNA biogenesis, stress-responsive signaling, inflammatory pathways, hypoxia/angiogenesis, and cell-cycle regulation. CONCLUSIONS: These findings define an exploratory plasma miRNA pattern in treatment-naïve PPMS and provide a biologically coherent shortlist for independent validation. Larger, longitudinal studies are required before diagnostic or mechanistic conclusions can be drawn.

title: Comment on "Prevalence and clinical associations of sleep-disordered breathing in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis".
Cognitive level and rate of change in relapsing and progressive multiple sclerosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study in Japan.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although secondary and primary progressive multiple sclerosis (MS) are associated with poorer cross-sectional cognition than relapsing MS, whether decline is faster remains uncertain. We examined associations of phenotype with cognitive performance and annual change. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 37 patients with MS underwent serial assessment using the Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT), Japanese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-J), and Frontal Assessment Battery (FAB) (161 observations; 144 for SDMT). Phenotype at the first assessment was retained throughout follow-up. Linear mixed-effects models included random intercepts and slopes and were adjusted for baseline age, sex, education, and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score; time was mean-centered. RESULTS: At baseline, 26 patients had relapsing and 11 had progressive disease. Mean follow-up was 4.2 years. The progressive group scored lower than the relapsing group: SDMT, -14.18 points (95% confidence interval [CI]: -25.00, -3.35); MoCA-J, -3.25 (-5.65, -0.85); FAB, -1.80 (-3.18, -0.43). Phenotype-by-time interactions were non-significant (SDMT: -0.87 points per year [95% CI: -2.03, 0.29]; MoCA-J: -0.24 [-0.54, 0.06]; FAB: -0.14 [-0.35, 0.08]). CONCLUSION: Progressive MS was associated with lower cognitive performance after adjustment for baseline EDSS score, without evidence of different rates of change. Lower MoCA-J and FAB scores in progressive MS have rarely been documented in Japanese patients. Larger cohorts with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether rates differ.

title: AIM2 as a therapeutic target in autoimmunity: balancing inflammasome inhibition with immune homeostasis.
abstract: Absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) is a cytosolic pattern recognition receptor that functions as a critical sensor of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) of microbial or host origin. Upon DNA recognition, AIM2 assembles into a multiprotein inflammasome complex that drives pyroptotic cell death and maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18. Beyond its canonical role in host defense, aberrant AIM2 activation by self-DNA has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of various inflammatory autoimmune diseases. This comprehensive review synthesizes current understanding of AIM2 biology. We examine the role of AIM2 in different immune cell populations, its effects on multiple downstream signaling pathways, and its complex association with autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and multiple sclerosis. Finally, we discussed therapeutic prospects and remaining challenges in targeting AIM2 for the treatment of autoimmunity.

title: Diffusion MRI reveals stage-dependent microstructural responses to early ferroptosis inhibition in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurodegeneration drives irreversible disability in multiple sclerosis (MS). Ferroptosis has been implicated in MS and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), but its spatiotemporal dynamics and imaging correlates remain unclear. METHODS: We combined 7.0 T diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) with histopathological and molecular analyses to evaluate the effects of Liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1) in mice with EAE induced by myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein peptide 35-55 (MOG35-55). Sixty-five female C57BL/6 mice were assigned to control, EAE, early-treatment (Early-Tx; Lip-1 from day 12), and late-treatment (Late-Tx; Lip-1 from day 18) groups. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and tissue analyses were performed at days 20 and 30 post-immunization. RESULTS: Early-Tx reduced clinical severity at day 30 (vs. EAE; p < 0.001) and limited body weight loss. At peak disease, voxel- and ROI-based DTI showed increased mean diffusivity and radial diffusivity in the corpus callosum, internal capsule, and thalamus, which were attenuated by Early-Tx. At the chronic stage, EAE showed persistent fractional anisotropy reduction in periventricular white matter and corpus callosum, whereas Early-Tx largely prevented these abnormalities. Histology demonstrated that Early-Tx suppressed inflammatory infiltration, microglial activation, and demyelination while preserving myelin integrity. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) upregulation and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation preceded overt iron deposition, whereas iron accumulation emerged mainly at the chronic stage and colocalized with activated microglia and demyelinated lesions. CONCLUSIONS: Ferroptosis-related molecular alterations are associated with stage-dependent inflammatory demyelinating injury in EAE. Early Lip-1 treatment provides greater microstructural protection than delayed treatment. High-field DTI sensitively detects treatment-responsive microstructural injury and may help monitor ferroptosis-related pathology in demyelinating disease.

title: Neuroinflammatory and demyelinating disorders in children: demystifying and updating with a focus on myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease.
abstract: Pediatric neuroinflammatory disorders are a heterogeneous group of autoimmune conditions that have evolved rapidly over the past decade and are encountered in both community and specialized pediatric practice. This group can share overlapping features and includes pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS), acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), formally defined by international consensus in 2023 [32]. Advances in imaging techniques, international consensus statements, and improved detection of central nervous system (CNS)-specific autoantibodies have enabled prompt, precise diagnosis of these disorders [2]. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential tool for early identification, differentiation, and diagnosis, enabling early intervention and focused treatment. This review provides an up-to-date clinico-radiological summary of pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), emphasizing MRI protocols and advanced sequences for lesion detection and phenotypic differentiation.

title: Mixed pain in multiple sclerosis: Beyond mechanistic classification toward clinical phenotyping.
Same biomarker, different number: why multiple sclerosis needs assay-aware NfL interpretation.
abstract: Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is moving from research into routine multiple sclerosis (MS) care, but the clinical meaning of a result depends partly on how that result was generated. Different specimen matrices and analytical platforms can preserve biological and clinical associations while producing non-interchangeable absolute concentrations. This matters particularly during longitudinal follow-up, where a platform change may mimic a biological change and affect interpretation near cut-offs or percentiles. We argue that analytical continuity should be treated as part of clinical continuity. NfL interpretation should explicitly integrate four domains-Biology, Method, Context and Action-and should prioritise patient-specific trajectories over isolated values. When possible, specimen matrix and analytical platform should be preserved; when the assay changes, the change should be documented and a new baseline considered. Making analytical metadata visible in the laboratory report is a practical step towards safer biomarker-guided neurology.

title: Mapping the prevalence of Epstein-Barr virus and multiple sclerosis in Middle East and North Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) prevalence has increased to medium-to-high levels in several countries of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), while Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) exposure as one of the most consistently reported MS risk factors is common throughout the region. This systematic review and meta-analysis descriptively mapped published estimates of MS prevalence and EBV seroprevalence alongside each other in MENA countries. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science until 18 June 2022. Observational studies reporting MS prevalence or EBV seroprevalence among healthy MENA populations were eligible. For quantitative EBV synthesis, we restricted analyses to studies reporting VCA-IgG seroprevalence to improve comparability across studies. Studies reporting the prevalence of specific type of MS or those assessing EBV infection by IgA antibodies or non-serological tissues or without a control arm representing general population were excluded. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools were used to determine the quality of the studies. The heterogeneity of studies was evaluated using I2 statistics. Results of the fix-effects meta-analysis were presented using prevalence and 95% confidence intervals. Of 4,323 records identified, 131 studies were included. The pooled MS prevalence was 51.02 per 100,000 population, and the pooled EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence was 75%. In time-stratified analyses, pooled MS prevalence increased from 12 per 100,000 in studies conducted up to 2000 to 58 per 100,000 in studies conducted from 2011 to 2022. Pooled EBV seroprevalence increased from 71 to 75% across the same periods. These findings suggest that the prevalence of both MS and EBV has increased over time, with a more pronounced increase observed for MS. Between-study heterogeneity was extreme for both outcomes (I2 = 100%), reflecting substantial variation in geography, populations, study methods, diagnostic approaches, and study periods. Published MS prevalence estimates and EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence estimates showed co-occurring uprising patterns in the available MENA literature. Based on a probable ecological correlation between the increasing prevalence of MS and EBV, the preventive measures against EBV infection may potentially yield favorable outcomes in terms of MS prevention. Future longitudinal, population-based studies with standardized MS ascertainment and age-specific EBV serology are needed.

title: Interferon Regulatory Factor 8 Drives Autoimmune Neuroinflammation in Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. The interferon regulatory factor (IRF) family comprises transcription factors that regulate immune responses; however, their roles in MS pathogenesis remain unclear. In this study, we investigated whether IRFs are involved in MS pathology using experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model mice. Among the IRFs examined, IRF8 expression was significantly increased in the spinal cord of EAE model mice and predominantly localized to myeloid cells. Consistently, patients with MS exhibited significantly increased proportions of IRF8-positive myeloid cells in peripheral blood. Notably, IRF8 knockout mice exhibited complete resistance to EAE induction. The mRNA expression levels of neuroinflammatory mediators, including interleukin IL-1β, IL-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, IL-12b, and nitric oxide synthase 2, were significantly reduced in the spinal cord of IRF8 knockout mice. Collectively, these findings suggest that IRF8 is a critical regulator of autoimmune neuroinflammation, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for MS.

title: Diet quality, gut microbiome diversity, and clinical disability in multiple sclerosis: A cross-sectional case-control study.
abstract: Dietary patterns and gut microbiome composition are increasingly recognised as modifiable factors in multiple sclerosis (MS). We aimed to evaluate dietary quality, microbiome diversity, and their inter-relationships with MS status, clinical disability, and disease-modifying therapy (DMT). We compared 288 MS cases with 274 household healthy controls (HHC). Dietary intake was assessed using healthy eating index (HEI-2015), and the groups were compared and associations analysed using multivariable linear regression. Among all HEI-2015 components, only total fruit intake was significantly higher in MS (β=+0.46; 95% CI: +0.19 to +0.74; FDR q = 0.014). Higher HEI-2015 scores were positively associated with greater Shannon alpha diversity (β=+0.077/10-unit increment; 95% CI: +0.003 to +0.150; p = 0.042). The PERMANOVA revealed independent association between microbiome beta diversity and smoking (R²=0.011; p = 0.007), BMI (R²=0.007; p = 0.010), age (R²=0.006; p = 0.027), and MS status (R²=0.005; p = 0.026), but not with diet quality (R²=0.006; p = 0.171). The whole grains consumption was directly associated with EDSS (FDR q = 0.033). Microbial richness differed across DMT categories (p = 0.001), and mechanism-level analysis attributed this to natalizumab, anti-CD20 therapy and dimethyl fumarate. In conclusion, higher fruit intake and dietary quality positively were related to gut microbiome diversity in MS. Disease status, smoking, and BMI are the primary drivers of microbiome community composition. Therefore, dietary modification could be a potential adjunctive strategy in MS management.

title: Baseline miR-10a, miR-146a, and miR-155 expression and subsequent clinical and radiological outcomes in multiple sclerosis: A retrospective observational study.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, immune-mediated central nervous system disorder with a multifactorial etiology, driven by genetic-environmental interplay. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), small non-coding RNAs, act as key post-transcriptional regulators within epigenetic mechanisms, integrating these determinants into gene expression networks. Increasing evidence implicates miRNA dysregulation as an important contributor to MS pathogenesis and progression. Between 2015 and 2018, expression levels of miR-10a, miR-146a, and miR-155 were obtained from whole blood samples of patients with MS using RT-PCR and evaluated to investigate associations between baseline miRNA expression patterns and subsequent clinical and radiological outcomes. Based on these data, the medical records of 54 patients who remained under follow-up (2015-2023) were reviewed retrospectively. Following expression analysis, the number of relapses, annualized relapse rate, changes in Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score, radiological activity, and achievement of No Evidence of Disease Activity (NEDA-3) status were assessed over a mean follow-up period of approximately 5 years. A total of 54 patients (40 female and 14 male) were included. The mean follow-up period was 62.44 ± 21.14 months (14-81 months). The median age at diagnosis was 31 years (16-53 years). Differences in miR-10a expression levels were found in 37 patients (68.5%), miR-146a in 36 (66.7%), and miR-155 in 41 (75.9%). miR-10a dysregulation was significantly associated with the final EDSS score (P = .007) and the presence of cervical spinal cord lesions at baseline (P = .040). miR-146a and miR-155 dysregulation were significantly associated with the development of new cervical spinal cord lesions (P = .020 and P = .025, respectively). miR-155 also showed a nominal association with overall radiological activity (P = .049). Exploratory ROC analysis showed limited discriminatory performance of miR-155 for radiological activity (AUC = 0.655, 95% CI: 0.513-0.779; P = .0387). In this exploratory retrospective study, baseline expression patterns of miR-10a, miR-146a, and miR-155 were associated with selected subsequent clinical and radiological outcomes in patients with MS. Associations were observed between miR-10a and disability measures, between miR-146a/miR-155 and new cervical spinal cord lesions, and between miR-155 and radiological activity. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger prospective studies with longitudinal miRNA assessment and independent validation.

title: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate measurement properties of Observational gait analysis (OGA) tools among neurological populations. METHODS: PRISMA-COSMIN guidelines were followed. Articles included measurement properties studies for OGA tools in neurologic populations were included. Studies were rated as sufficient, insufficient, or indeterminate. Results were synthesized by the population and OGA tool. RESULTS: Twenty-eight included articles performed 63 studies for 7 OGA tools that were synthesized in 42 results in stroke, multiple sclerosis and Parkison's disease. The Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), and Gait Assessment and Intervention tool (G.A.I.T) in stroke have been studied for all properties except measurement invariance, and all of them were sufficient except measurement error. Other OGA tools were tested in limited studies. All included tools have potential for recommendation; however, none was fully recommended for use. CONCLUSION: WGS and G.A.I.T in stroke have the best potential for recommendation. They can be used at only group-level or cross-sectional analysis due to their large measurement error. Standardized observation methods and measurement invariance studies should be prioritized. Both WGS and G.A.I.T measure gait deviations through 14 and 31 items respectively, WGS provides more feasible assessment while G.A.I.T provides more detailed biomechanical analysis.

title: Food insecurity and pain burden in patients with multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis: A comparative case-control study.
abstract: BackgroundFood insecurity (FI) is strongly associated with chronic disease diagnoses, pain, and functional decline. Patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have been reported to experience some degree of FI.AimsTo assess and compare the prevalence of FI in patients with MS and RA and examine associations between FI, disease severity, disability, and pain.MethodsA comparative case-control design was adopted, including 40 patients with MS and 40 patients with RA. FI was assessed using the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale (HFIAS), and pain was evaluated using the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI). Disease severity was measured using the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) for MS and the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints (DAS28) for RA. Group comparisons were performed, and multivariable regression analyses were conducted to examine associations between FI, pain, disease activity, and demographic factors.SummaryFI was identified in 65% of patients with MS and 37.5% of those with RA (p = 0.014). Patients with MS had greater odds of exhibiting FI compared to those with RA (p = 0.028). In multivariable analyses among patients with MS, greater disability was associated with increased FI (p = 0.019). In contrast, among those with RA, disease activity was not associated with FI. In pooled sample analyses, greater FI was independently associated with both pain severity (p = 0.027) and pain interference (p = 0.009). Overall, FI is prevalent among patients with MS and RA, with a greater prevalence observed in MS. Greater FI was consistently associated with increased pain severity and interference. These findings highlight the importance of routine FI screening and tailored nutritional and social support interventions in vulnerable populations.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in neurology: biomarkers and clinical implications.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a shared downstream pathogenic mechanism across a wide spectrum of neurological disorders, ranging from primary mitochondrial diseases to conditions including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis, hereditary ataxias and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. This Review examines the role of mitochondrial biomarkers in improving diagnostic accuracy, patient stratification and monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response. Primary mitochondrial diseases are presented as proof-of-concept models of impaired oxidative phosphorylation, providing a framework for biomarker identification and validation with translational relevance to other neurological diseases. Mitochondrial biomarkers can be broadly categorized into four domains: fluid biomarkers, reflecting metabolic alterations and stress signalling; genetic biomarkers, capturing mitochondrial DNA integrity and dynamics; multi-omics approaches, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures; and imaging biomarkers, enabling in vivo assessment of structural and functional consequences of mitochondrial dysfunction. Across disorders, these biomarkers reveal shared disturbances in bioenergetics, redox homeostasis, mitochondrial genome maintenance and inflammatory signalling. However, clinical implementation remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, biological variability and reduced disease specificity. Integrated, multimodal biomarker strategies, combined with longitudinal validation, will be essential for supporting precision medicine and guiding the development of therapies to target mitochondrial pathways in neurology.

title: Cellular senescence in ageing and neurodegenerative disorders: Molecular mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Cellular senescence has been increasingly associated with neurodegenerative disorders, potentially linking ageing-related cellular impairment with mitochondrial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and disrupted intercellular signalling. The present study aims to explore the increasing relevance of cellular senescence among key cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, neural progenitor cells, microglia and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells across neurodegenerative ailments such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and multiple sclerosis. This review discusses the findings of pre-clinical and clinical studies which suggest that senescence-associated features may contribute to neurodegeneration. Further, it provides an overview of the biomarkers used in the identification of senescence in the CNS. Also, the review examines senotherapeutic treatment approaches, highlighting their actions on different CNS cell types and the growing clinical evidence. It also points out the challenges in translating these approaches to clinical application, such as targeting specific cell types and the lack of suitable biomarkers. Collectively, present findings suggest that senescence-associated alterations may contribute to neurodegeneration, although their effects appear to vary across cell types and diseases.

title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. METHODS: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting. FINDINGS: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns. INTERPRETATION: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis. FUNDING: Novartis.

title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression.
abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

title: Construct validity and intrasession intra-rater reliability of the stair and step tests in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This research aimed to establish the test-retest reliability, agreement, measurement precision, and construct validity of the Stair and Step Tests in individuals with Multiple Sclerosis (MS). METHODS: One hundred patients with MS were evaluated using the Stair Test, Step Test, Timed Up and Go (TUG), 30-Second Chair Stand Test (30-s CSTS), Modified Four Square Step Test (mFSST), and 12-Item MS Walking Scale (MSWS-12). For test-retest reliability, the Stair and Step Tests were repeated after a 60-minute rest. Data were analyzed for reliability (ICC2,1), agreement (Bland-Altman), measurement precision (SEM95, MDC95), and construct validity (Pearson correlations). RESULTS: Both assessments demonstrated excellent test-retest reliability. The Stair Test achieved an ICC2,1 of 0.997 (95% CI: 0.996-0.998), while the Step Test reached 0.955 (95% CI: 0.933-0.969). Regarding measurement precision, SEM95 and MDC95 were 0.15; 0.41 for the Stair Test, and 0.58; 1.61 for the Step Test. Bland-Altman analysis revealed tight agreement with negligible bias for the Stair (-0.003) and Step (0.030) tests. The Stair Test correlated strongly with TUG, mFSST, MSWS-12, and EDSS (all r = 0.979), and inversely with 30-s CSTS (r =  -0.957) (p < .01). The Step Test showed positive associations with 30-s CSTS (r = 0.908) and inverse links to TUG (r =  -0.929), mFSST (r =  -0.929), MSWS-12 (r =  -0.927), and EDSS (r =  -0.928) (p < .01). CONCLUSION: The Stair and Step Tests offer a clinically practical, fast, and low-fatigue solution for monitoring mobility in MS, bridging the gap between psychometric precision and the time constraints of routine physiotherapy practice.

title: Divergent Trends in Relapse Activity and Relapse-Independent Progression Over Two Decades in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Multiple sclerosis (MS) management has increasingly favored earlier high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy (DMT). We examined diagnosis-era changes in relapse activity and disability accrual alongside evolving DMT use. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed two Italian cohorts of adults with MS onset in 2001-2024 across four diagnosis eras. Annualized relapse rate (ARR) was modeled by Poisson regression; confirmed disability accrual (CDA), relapse-associated worsening (RAW), and progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) by Andersen-Gill Cox models. CDA was classified as RAW when relapse onset occurred from 90 days before through 30 days after the event, otherwise as PIRA. Treatment was time-varying: untreated, low-/moderate-efficacy therapy (LET/MET), or high-efficacy therapy (HET). Inverse probability-weighted models included residual adjustment. Sensitivity analyses examined a strict common 2-year horizon, MRI restriction/adjustment, relapsing-onset MS, first-event analyses, 90-day DMT lag, early-HET exclusion, pre-treatment versus never-treated person-time, visit frequency, and center stratification. RESULTS: Among 1096 patients (228, 214, 292, and 362 across eras 1-4), first-line HET use reached 45.9% in era 4. Each later diagnosis year was associated with lower ARR (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99; p < 0.001), with steeper calendar-time declines during LET/MET and HET than untreated person-time (joint interaction p < 0.001). Later diagnosis year was also associated with lower RAW (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.97; p < 0.001) and modestly lower CDA over full follow-up (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00; p = 0.026), although CDA attenuated in weighted and common-horizon analyses. PIRA was not associated with diagnosis year (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.99-1.04; p = 0.262). Lower ARR and RAW persisted across sensitivities, whereas the strict 2-year analysis suggested higher early PIRA in more recent eras. CONCLUSION: Later diagnosis-era cohorts had lower relapse activity and relapse-associated disability accrual, whereas overall disability accrual was less consistent and PIRA did not decline. Improvements in relapse-related disease activity were not accompanied by a comparable reduction in relapse-independent disability accrual.

title: Availability of resources to apply the 2024 McDonald criteria: A global perspective.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 3rd ECTRIMS Winter School highlighted regional and global disparities in resources needed to implement the 2024 McDonald diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis. OBJECTIVES: To assess the availability of paraclinical tools and regional differences in access reported by neurologists in an online survey. RESULTS: The survey was completed by 328 neurologists from 44 countries. Core diagnostic tools, including magnetic resonance imaging and oligoclonal band testing, were widely available. Access to advanced imaging, optic nerve assessment, and laboratory biomarkers varied across regions. CONCLUSIONS: Variability in access to key paraclinical tests may impact on the implementation of the 2024 McDonald criteria globally.

title: Prediction of short-term and long-term responses to cladribine in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: a Danish nationwide real-world study.
abstract: Cladribine is regarded highly efficacious in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). However, prediction of treatment response and optimal management remain elusive, particularly during long-term. We screened the Danish Multiple Sclerosis Registry for patients with RRMS who received ≥2 5-day treatment cycles of cladribine and were followed for >90 days. Annualised relapse rates (ARR) and activity parameters (relapses or MRI activity) were analysed from 90 days after the first dose (index) to year 3 (short-term) together with time-to-first 24-week confirmed disability worsening (CDW), CDW independent of relapses (PIRA), and activity/CDW (loss of "no evidence of disease activity", NEDA-3). Kaplan-Meier log-rank tests were validated in a subgroup who completed ≥4 five-day cladribine cycles before year 3 and contributed with >3 years follow-up (3YFS). Predicting covariables included age (< /≥ 45 years), pre-baseline activity, and short-term NEDA-3 status regarding 3YFS outcomes beyond year 3 (long-term). ARR declined significantly from ~0.55 in the year pre-baseline to ~0.23-0.25 from index to year 3. Younger age and pre-baseline activity predicted more frequent short-term activity. Pre-baseline activity additionally predicted short-term NEDA-3 loss. Short-term findings were consistent in 3YFS patients. CDW and PIRA were rare during short-term (~ 10%) and long-term (~ 20%), even in older patients. However, during long-term, NEDA-3 loss resumed steadily and this was largely unpredictable. While cladribine showed sustained short-term efficacy, treatment response appeared more favourable in older patients and patients without pre-baseline activity. Rare CDW and PIRA events warrant more research in cladribine for disability prevention. Optimal long-term management following cladribine treatment requires more research.

title: DELPHI expert consensus-derived factors influencing the early use of monoclonal high-efficacy therapies in treatment-naïve patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To gather expert consensus regarding initiation of monoclonal high-efficacy therapies (HET) amongst treatment-naïve relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) patients in France. METHODS: The study leveraged the Delphi method to gauge consensus amongst an expert panel of 31 neurologists. Eight clinical cases with demographic, clinical and imaging characteristics were presented, prompting the experts to respond if they would recommend monoclonal HET. Additionally, potentially influential parameters were changed one at a time to assess whether the experts would recommend monoclonal HET. After a first round, an e-workshop was conducted to discuss non-consensual statements, which were re-submitted for rating (Round 2). Characteristics influencing monoclonal HET initiation were evaluated. RESULTS: 31/31 experts responded to both rounds. Consensus for or against monoclonal HET was reached for 89/108 (82.4%) statements. Factors that systematically led to monoclonal HET initiation were high brain lesion load (>20 lesions), ≥2 spinal cord lesions, ≥3 gadolinium-enhancing lesions and ≥3 infratentorial lesions. A single spinal cord lesion, in combination with other factors (which, in isolation, often but not always led to monoclonal HET), systematically led to monoclonal HET recommendation. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that the panel of French neurologists favoured monoclonal HET initiation amongst treatment-naïve RRMS patients with high radiological disease activity, whereas clinical characteristics played a complementary role.

title: Risk of Inflammatory Bowel Disease After Anti-CD20 Treatment in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Anti-CD20 biologics are widely used as disease-modifying therapy (DMT) for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), but recent reports have raised concerns about an increased risk of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) during treatment. This study aimed to assess treatment-associated IBD risk in individuals with RRMS. OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of new-onset IBD across different therapies for RRMS and relative to the general population. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a population-based cohort study conducted in Sweden. Through the Swedish MS register, initiations of rituximab, natalizumab, dimethyl fumarate, and fingolimod were identified between January 1, 2011, and December 31, 2023, in individuals with RRMS aged 18 to 55 years with at least 10 years of lookback time (5 years for dispensed drugs) and no evidence of previous IBD. These initiations were matched with general population comparator episodes selected from the Swedish population. EXPOSURES: Rituximab, comparator DMTs (natalizumab, dimethyl fumarate, fingolimod), or general population comparator. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: New-onset IBD, defined as 2 or more records on separate dates with the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision, codes K50 (Crohn disease), K51 (ulcerative colitis), and/or K52.3 (indeterminate colitis). RESULTS: Among the 13 748 therapy episodes (6481 rituximab, 2976 natalizumab, 2767 dimethyl fumarate, 1524 fingolimod) in 9251 individuals (range in mean ages of the exposure groups, 35-38 years) and 61 065 matched general population episodes, 164 IBD events occurred during follow-up (40 with rituximab, 4 with comparator DMTs, and 120 in the general population). The crude incidence rate of IBD was 110 (95% CI, 76-147) per 100 000 person-years for rituximab, 13 (95% CI, 3-30) for the comparator DMTs, and 41 (95% CI, 34-48) for the general population. After adjustment for demographics and MS characteristics, the hazard ratio for the comparator DMTs vs rituximab was 0.10 (95% CI, 0.04-0.22). In the rituximab group, 62% of IBD events were classified as Crohn disease compared with 29% in the general population. The number needed to harm for rituximab vs the comparator DMTs was 131 (95% CI, 93-228) at 5 years, after full adjustment. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study show that rituximab was associated with an increased risk of IBD compared with other modern MS therapies, after adjustment for differences in characteristics at therapy start. Clinicians and individuals with MS should consider IBD risk in treatment decisions and remain vigilant for gastrointestinal symptoms during anti-CD20 therapy.

title: Subjective Sleep Quality in Relation to Relapse Status in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Nested Case-Control Analysis.
abstract: Background: Sleep disturbance is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), but its relationship with relapse status remains insufficiently defined. This study examined whether poorer subjective sleep quality was associated with relapse status in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. Methods: This propensity score-matched nested case-control analysis included 132 patients with relapsing-remitting MS selected from 473 consecutively evaluated patients at a tertiary multiple sclerosis centre. Patients in relapse were matched 1:1 to patients in remission by age, sex, disease duration, Expanded Disability Status Scale score, disease-modifying therapy duration and efficacy class, and relapse in the previous year. Sleep quality and related symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires. Results: Patients in relapse were more frequently classified as poor sleepers than those in remission (59.1% vs. 36.4%; p = 0.009). In the double-adjusted logistic regression model, higher Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores were independently associated with relapse status (OR = 1.16; 95% CI 1.02-1.32; p = 0.023), whereas the remaining variables were not independently associated with relapse status. Conclusions: Poorer subjective sleep quality was independently associated with relapse status in relapsing-remitting MS, supporting sleep disturbance as a relapse-associated clinical feature rather than a proven causal risk factor.

title: A Qualitative Analysis of Focus Groups on a Community-Based Pro Bono Exercise and Lifestyle Modification Education Program for Individuals With Disability due to Multiple Sclerosis and Stroke.
abstract: The aim of this study was to identify perceived logistical, behavioral, and practical barriers to regular exercise participation in individuals with disability due to stroke and multiple sclerosis, as well as potential solutions. Focus group interviews were conducted as part of a mixed-methods prospective observational study evaluating a multi-site, pro bono, community-based exercise and lifestyle modification program. Twelve participants engaged in one of three focus groups, and data analysis was conducted using a modified grounded theory approach. Five themes were identified through thematic analysis: fear of exercising and need for safety when implementing an exercise program; personal experiences of physical and mental health and wellness; importance of social support and sense of community foster accountability and camaraderie; role of self-efficacy in daily life participation and resilience; and accessibility of fitness centers. Key factors were identified that influence exercise participation among individuals with disability due to neurological diagnosis. Overall, strong motivation to enhance overall health and wellbeing was observed; however, safety concerns and accessibility were barriers to participation. Social support and a sense of community were identified as critical factors to foster accountability and engagement. Despite existing barriers, building self-efficacy and resilience emerged as powerful enablers of long-term participation in exercise.

title: Family planning in multiple sclerosis: An Australian perspective.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based, Australia-specific recommendations for managing multiple sclerosis (MS) before conception, during pregnancy and after birth, balancing maternal health, disease control, and fetal safety. METHODS: A panel of seven Australian MS specialists, from academic and clinical backgrounds, convened (April-October 2025) via virtual meetings and email correspondence. A targeted literature review covered MS, pregnancy, postpartum relapse, breastfeeding, vaccination and disease-modifying therapy safety. Guidance from the Therapeutic Goods Administration, international clinical guidelines, and safety data were examined to inform interpretation. RESULTS: Evidence indicates that MS does not increase adverse pregnancy outcomes, although a higher risk of small-for-gestational-age birth may occur. Treatment selection should account for teratogenicity and rebound risk. Teriflunomide, fingolimod, siponimod and cladribine require cessation well before conception and are contraindicated during breastfeeding. Natalizumab can be continued until conception and through the first and second trimesters using extended-interval dosing; postpartum resumption is advised to minimise rebound relapses. Ofatumumab and ocrelizumab should be stopped if pregnancy is confirmed. Treatment decisions should be individualised through shared decision-making. European Union guidance supports use of ocrelizumab during breastfeeding, consistent with evidence of minimal monoclonal antibody transfer into breastmilk. As breastfeeding does not prevent relapse, early postpartum DMT resumption is recommended to reduce relapse risk. Contraceptive use remains low despite requirements for many therapies. CONCLUSION: With proactive planning, women with MS can achieve optimal pregnancy outcomes. This consensus integrates evidence, regulatory considerations and Australian guidance to support a practical framework for family planning in MS.

title: The reported pain-cognition dissociation in multiple sclerosis: different pain scores for objective and perceived cognition.
Salivary Proteomics Reveals Disease- and Therapy-Associated Molecular Patterns in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune-mediated disease for which non-invasive biomarkers, able to detect disease- and treatment-associated molecular changes, are needed. We characterized the whole-saliva proteome of patients with relapsing-remitting (RR) MS at baseline before treatment initiation (MS-T0; n = 66) and after six months of disease-modifying therapy (MS-T1; n = 40), in comparison with healthy controls (HC; n = 31). Nano-liquid chromatography-high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry identified 1305 proteins, of which 209 differed among the main comparisons. Pairwise and paired analyses distinguished persistent RRMS-associated alterations, baseline-attenuation patterns with changes shifting towards HC levels, treatment-associated differences emerging at MS-T1, and longitudinal-only alterations. The identified patterns are descriptive and cannot be interpreted as evidence of pharmacological treatment effects or clinical response. The existence of specific RRMS alterations was supported by exploratory Random Forest, which classified HC, MS-T0 and MS-T1 samples using a panel of 50 proteins, most of which (96%) also showed significant changes in univariate tests. Reactome enrichment evidenced that proteins pertaining to the identified patterns are mainly involved in innate immunity, neutrophil degranulation, cell-death pathways, cytokine signalling, and protein folding. These findings indicate that six months of therapy was associated with substantial salivary proteome changes and support saliva as a candidate biofluid for longitudinal molecular monitoring and non-invasive detection of treatment-associated salivary proteome variations in RRMS.

title: Brain-Computer Interfaces for Cognitive Rehabilitation: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Cognitive diseases/disorders are a major cause of disability affecting millions of people worldwide due to pathologies or conditions such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, vascular cognitive impairment, and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder. The effects of these diseases/disorders can range from subjective cognitive complaints to mild cognitive impairment and even dementia that can affect multiple cognitive domains, causing disability and alterations in daily functioning and quality of life. Cognitive training has been researched as a potential therapeutic option for treating cognitive disability. In particular, cognitive training delivered using brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) represents a promising technology for cognitive rehabilitation. For this reason, this work presents a narrative review aimed at bridging the clinical aspects of cognition performance and the technical features of BCI systems. Additionally, it reports on the current advances of BCIs for cognitive rehabilitation in the pathologies/conditions that are the main contributors of cognitive impairment globally. Specifically, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, mild cognitive impairment, cerebrovascular diseases, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder were included in the review; other pathologies that can also cause cognitive impairment such as multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, brain tumors, infectious diseases, and psychiatric conditions such as schizophrenia or autism spectrum disorder, or drug or toxin-related causes were outside the scope of the present review. Across the literature, studies have reported that BCI cognitive training can improve cognition performance for mild cognitive impairment, stroke, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, showcasing its feasibility as a complementary therapy. However, the amount of evidence is still scarce, with few reported randomized controlled clinical trials and all of the applications comprising non-invasive systems using electroencephalography, while invasive or other non-invasive approaches remain largely unassessed. Therefore, further research regarding the design of BCIs for targeting specific cognitive domains is necessary to allow for the future introduction of these types of systems into clinical rehabilitation environments, rather than only demonstrating their feasibility, as has been mainly done to date.

title: Impact of newly diagnosed multiple sclerosis on marital status and partner relationship.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on short-term impact of multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis on intimate relationships remains limited. This study investigated the perceived impact of MS diagnosis on relationship status within the first year following diagnosis. METHODS: This survey-based observational study used data from the Swiss Multiple Sclerosis Registry (SMSR). Factors potentially associated with perceived MS direct impact on relationship status within the first year after diagnosis were explored using logistic regression. Among participants reporting that MS impacted their relationship, we explored changes in relationship status and factors associated with relationship dissolution. RESULTS: Among 881 participants included (74% female), 453 were married, 235 with a partner, and 193 single at diagnosis. Overall, 89 participants (10.1%) reported that MS diagnosis impacted their relationship (i.e., 6.2% of married; 14.5% of partnered; 14% of single). Compared with married participants, partnered (ORadj 2.3; 95%CI 1.30-4.06) and single participants (ORadj 2.26; 95%CI 1.25-4.07) were more likely to report impact. Cognitive symptoms were associated with higher odds of reporting impact (ORadj 2.02, 95%CI 1.28-3.19). Among married participants, primary progressive MS was associated with increased odds of relationship impact (ORadj 3.21; 95%CI 1.15-8.33). Among partnered participants, men were more likely than women to report an impacted relationship (ORadj 3.00; 95%CI 1.23-7.25). Among participants with reported relationship impact, relationship trajectories included continuation, strengthening, and dissolution. None of the studied factors were associated with relationship dissolution. CONCLUSION: One in ten participants reported MS diagnosis impacting their relationship, and consequent relationship changes were heterogeneous, suggesting that this influence may belong to broader psychosocial processes.

title: Real-world treatment in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis: Data from the Swiss pediatric inflammatory brain disease cohort study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) exhibits more aggressive inflammation than adult-onset multiple sclerosis, with higher relapse rates, faster lesion accrual, earlier disability progression, and a greater risk of cognitive impairment. Appropriate treatment is crucial to minimize lifelong impairment. METHODS: This multicenter, observational cohort study examined patients from the Swiss Pediatric Inflammatory Brain Disease Registry with POMS who received index treatment with disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) of varying efficacy: mild-efficacy therapy (MET), intermediate-efficacy therapy (IET), and high-efficacy therapy (HET). We analyzed demographic and baseline characteristics, index treatment type, reasons for switching, breakthrough disease activity, and pre- and post-treatment annualized relapse rates before and after index treatment start.
