We further studied index treatment prescription development over time. Descriptive statistics were used. RESULTS: Of 41 patients with POMS, 32 (78%) were female. Thirty-nine received disease-modifying treatment post-diagnosis: 15 started MET, 13 IET, and 11 HET. Discontinuation was highest with MET (67%), followed by IET (54%), and HET (18%). Side effects prompted switching in the MET group, while disease activity drove switching in IET and HET groups. Mean annualized relapse rates decreased after index treatment from 1.07 to 0.43 with MET, from 1.17 to 0.33 with IET, and from 1.73 to 0.09 with HET. After 2019, MET was discontinued as index treatment. DISCUSSION: POMS treatment has evolved; since 2019, only IET and HET have been used in this Swiss cohort, achieving ARR reductions and lower discontinuation rates compared to MET.

title: Exercise-induced pain modulation in multiple sclerosis: Why pain phenotype matters.
Identification of BRD4 as a Shared Diagnostic Biomarker Between Bipolar Disorder and Multiple Sclerosis Using Machine Learning.
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is closely associated with multiple sclerosis (MS), but their shared molecular mechanisms and specific diagnostic biomarkers remain unclear. This study integrated microarray expression profiling and machine learning to identify shared core genes and underlying mechanisms between BD and MS. Gene expression datasets and peripheral-blood transcriptome datasets were obtained from the GEO database. After per-cohort quantile normalization, shared genes were identified by differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed, and key genes were screened using the MCODE plugin. Three machine learning algorithms were combined to identify the final core gene. A total of 229 shared genes were initially obtained and further filtered to 55 key genes.

title: Perceived Acceptability, Design Preferences, and User Requirements for a Proposed Ear-Worn Device for Heart-Rate and Ear-Temperature Monitoring with Localized Neck Cooling: A Pre-Prototype Mixed-Methods Study in People with Multiple Sclerosis.

Association Between Local Ascending Aortic Elastic Properties and Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Echocardiographic Study.
From Global Evidence to Saudi Practice: A Structured Evidence Map of the Diagnosis, Molecular Targets, and Therapeutic Strategies of Multiple Sclerosis in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has shifted in a generation from an uncommon diagnosis in Saudi Arabia to a major cause of neurological disability in young adults. Available Saudi data describe clinical characteristics broadly similar to those reported elsewhere in the Middle East and do not show that Saudi patients differ from trial populations, although this does not establish equivalent efficacy or safety. How far global advances are usable in the Kingdom has not, however, been synthesized. This narrative review maps diagnostic and therapeutic strategies across five separately reported domains (clinical evidence, 2022 national consensus listing, affordability, monitoring requirement, regional data), with categories assigned by a pre-specified rule, not a composite grade. Regional evidence on established therapies is entirely observational: cohorts report favourable outcomes with fingolimod, natalizumab, and off-label rituximab but cannot establish comparative effectiveness, and physicians report cost, availability, and insurance formularies as constraints whose extent has not been quantified. Diagnosis, now based on the 2024 McDonald revision, is transferable in knowledge but depends on AQP4-IgG testing, MRI, and biomarker capacity whose national distribution is undocumented, with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder an important differential. Tolebrutinib, recently approved in Europe for non-relapsing secondary progressive MS, and experimental modalities remain regulatory or research questions without regional data. Saudi studies document substantial payer costs of disease-modifying therapy, but none have measured how often cost or infrastructure alters treatment; we propose a prioritized research agenda.

title: DNA donation decisions, uncertainty, and perceived learning in a Serbian survey on multiple sclerosis genetics.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine willingness to donate DNA for multiple sclerosis (MS) research, with particular attention to uncertainty versus unwillingness, and perceived learning during completion of a questionnaire on MS genetics. METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey was conducted in Serbia. Regression analyses focused on the non-professional subsample. Multinomial logistic regression examined willing, unwilling, and insufficient-information responses to DNA donation, while multivariable linear regression examined perceived learning, measured by "I know now" responses to seven informational items. RESULTS: Among 1075 valid DNA-donation responses, 49.8% were willing, 22.9% lacked sufficient information to decide, and 27.3% were unwilling. In adjusted analyses, not wanting personal genetic risk information was more strongly associated with unwillingness than with uncertainty, while prior awareness of genetic data protection was associated with less uncertainty relative to both willingness and unwillingness. Respondents reported a median perceived-learning score of 5 out of 7. Greater objective knowledge and familiarity with MS were associated with higher perceived-learning scores, whereas male sex and age ≤ 20 years were associated with lower scores. CONCLUSION: Respondents who lacked sufficient information to decide about DNA donation differed from those who were unwilling to participate, supporting the treatment of uncertainty as a distinct response. The reported perceived learning also suggests that questionnaires incorporating informational content may provide an opportunity to support awareness alongside data collection. PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Research communication should distinguish insufficient information from refusal and clearly address personal genetic risk information and data protection. Informational questionnaires may complement these efforts, although their educational effects require objective evaluation.

title: Depressive symptoms and CSF markers of B-cell activation in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Psychiatric symptoms in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) may be considered as a biologically driven manifestation of the disease. B-cell activation is reliably reflected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by means of oligoclonal bands (OCBs) and the kappa free light chain (κ-FLC) index. We retrospectively explored the relationship of CSF OCBs and κ-FLC index with psychiatric symptoms in a consecutive series of newly diagnosed pwMS. Both OCB positivity and a κ-FLC index ≥3.3 were significantly associated with higher depressive symptoms scores. Multivariate analyses confirmed the association for OCB positivity and a borderline association for a κ-FLC index ≥3.3. Our findings support the need to systematically assess psychiatric symptoms in MS as a biologically based component of the disease.

title: Effects of Occupational Therapy Interventions on Occupational Performance and Physical and Cognitive Fatigue in Adults with Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Age-Stratified Comparison of Gait Biomechanics in People with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis and Healthy Individuals: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
abstract: Background and Objectives: Gait impairment is a common and disabling manifestation of multiple sclerosis, affecting mobility, independence, and quality of life. However, gait differences between people with multiple sclerosis and healthy individuals have not been well characterized within corresponding age strata. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional study included 23 participants with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and 50 healthy individuals aged 20-69 years. Participants underwent instrumented gait analysis at self-selected walking speed using a Vicon motion-capture system synchronized with force plates. Spatiotemporal parameters, lower-limb and pelvic kinematics, and ground reaction forces were assessed. Between-group comparisons were performed within predefined age strata (20-39, 40-49, 50-59, and 60-69 years) using one-dimensional Statistical Parametric Mapping and non-parametric analyses. Results: Across age strata, participants with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis generally showed slower walking and shorter stride-related measures, together with phase-specific multi-joint kinematic and ground reaction force deviations. Estimated gait-speed and stride-length differences were largest in the youngest stratum, whereas mean stride width was 0.04 m greater in both the youngest and oldest strata; however, confidence intervals were wide, and no between-stratum contrast was tested. Exploratory threshold crossings were not interpreted as evidence that the underlying effects differed among strata. Conclusions: The age-stratified, participant-level analysis identified recurrent differences in forward progression, lower-limb and pelvic kinematics, and loading and propulsion. These findings provide a quantitative description that may support individualized gait assessment and hypothesis generation for adequately powered studies. They do not establish an independent effect of age or an age-by-disease interaction.

title: Short term effect of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation of the medial sensorimotor cortex for neurogenic pelvic floor dysfunction in multiple sclerosis: a randomized, double blind, sham controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurogenic pelvic floor dysfunction, comprising bladder, bowel and sexual disturbance, affects most people with multiple sclerosis (MS) and responds poorly to pharmacotherapy. The medial sensorimotor cortex contains the pelvic floor representation, but controlled evidence for cortical neuromodulation in MS is scarce and bladder focused. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the short term efficacy and safety of inhibitory (1 Hz) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the vertex (Cz) in MS-related pelvic floor dysfunction. METHODS: Forty-five patients with definite MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) ≤6.0) and actionable bladder symptoms Screening Tool (ABSST≥8) were randomized 2:1 in a double-blind, sham-controlled single centre trial to active (n = 30) or sham (n = 15) stimulation: 1 Hz rTMS at 90-100% resting motor threshold (900 pulses) over Cz across 10 weekday sessions; sham used a 90° tilted coil with synchronized scalp electrodes. ABSST, Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction (NBD) score, Multiple Sclerosis Impact Scale 29(MSIS-29), Multiple Sclerosis Intimacy and Sexuality Questionnaire (MSISQ- 19), Overactive Bladder Questionnaire-Short Form (OAB -q SF) were assessed at baseline and 12 weeks post treatment. RESULTS: ABSST fell from 18.6 ± 4.5 to 13.9 ± 5.1 with active stimulation versus 17.8 ± 3.8 to 17.1 ± 3.5 with sham (ANCOVA adjusted difference -3.98, 95%CI -6.75 to -1.22; standardized effect -0.93; p = 0.006). After baseline and multiplicity adjustment, benefit persisted for bowel (NBD; FDR adjusted p = 0.004) and sexual (MSISQ-19; p = 0.036) domains, but not OAB-q SF or MSIS-29. Bladder improvement correlated with bowel (r = 0.464) and sexual (r = 0.374) improvement. No serious adverse events occurred. All 45 participants completed all ten sessions and the 12 week assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Inhibitory vertex rTMS produced sustained, coherent cross domain improvement in MS-related pelvic floor dysfunction exceeding sham, consistent with modulation of a shared central substrate and supports cortical neuromodulation as a promising, well tolerated adjunct.

title: Autoimmune comorbidity profiles in MOGAD and AQP4-NMOSD: a real-world evidence study of top 10 autoimmune disorders across the pre- and post-COVID-19 eras.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4-NMOSD) are antibody-mediated demyelinating disorders presenting with distinct immunopathogenic mechanisms. Systemic autoimmune comorbidity patterns and their evolution across the COVID-19 era remain incompletely characterized in real-world settings. We compared systemic autoimmune burdens and immune laboratory profiles between MOGAD and AQP4-NMOSD, systematically evaluating temporal changes before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Research Network (2015-2025). Antibody-confirmed cohorts included 2533 MOGAD and 453 AQP4-NMOSD patients (multiple sclerosis was strictly excluded). Ten systemic autoimmune categories were identified using ICD-10 codes. Immune laboratory markers, including antinuclear antibodies, anti-dsDNA, complement levels, and immunoglobulin dynamics, were analyzed. Temporal analyses included pre-/post-diagnosis windows and pre-/post-COVID-19 era stratification. RESULTS: AQP4-NMOSD patients were older and predominantly female compared to those with MOGAD. AQP4-NMOSD demonstrated a substantially higher baseline systemic autoimmune burden, including systemic lupus erythematosus (16%vs 1%), other connective tissue involvement (12%vs 5%), rheumatoid arthritis (6%vs 2%), and autoimmune gastrointestinal disease. Marked serum IgG reduction and post-diagnosis autoantibody titer resolution occurred predominantly in AQP4-NMOSD. COVID-era comparisons revealed persistent, high comorbidity odds in AQP4-NMOSD alongside selective temporal accrual of connective tissue, vascular, and thyroid comorbidities within MOGAD. CONCLUSION: AQP4-NMOSD is embedded within a broader humoral autoimmune network, whereas MOGAD exhibits a restricted systemic immune phenotype. The COVID-19 era accentuated preexisting subtype-specific architectures rather than uniformly increasing autoimmune burden. These findings support subtype-specific autoimmune surveillance strategies and reinforce precision phenotyping in antibody-mediated demyelinating disorders.

title: Ethmoid bone marrow region modulates lymphoid activation and differentiation with distinct myeloid profile in neuroinflammation.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: The skull bone marrow axis has recently emerged as an important source of immune cells during neuroinflammation, including in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), the mouse model of multiple sclerosis. The cribriform plate bone marrow (cpBM), is a portion of the ethmoid bone of the skull of mice, and is positioned next to nasal regions. At the cribriform plate olfactory nerves pass through the skull and recent evidence supports that it represents an important immune niche with links to CSF outflow and connections to cpBM. Previous data supports cellular composition of the ethmoid bone marrow in mice is altered in neuroinflammation suggesting it senses inflammatory cues, but the exact nature of these changes is still unclear. Here using scRNAseq and flow cytometry of the ethmoid bone marrow region we test how the region responds to EAE. In addition, we also compare the cpBM region with systemic bone marrow in the femur to understand region specific differences. We report that neuroinflammation creates a regulatory response at these sites and implicates the cpBM in controlling these effects. A better understanding of the cribriform niche may offer new treatments for neuroinflammatory disease.

title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing-Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study.
abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. To characterize taxonomic and functional gut microbiome differences between relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS) and their associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers. This cross-sectional study included 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 RRMS, and 30 SPMS). Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to assess microbial diversity, taxonomic profiles, and predefined short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-related pathways, integrated with disability measures and serum GFAP, NfL, and S100B. SPMS participants were substantially older than those with RRMS (median 49.0 vs. 31.0 years), prompting age-adjusted analyses and an age-overlap sensitivity analysis. Alpha diversity and overall microbial community composition were similar across groups. SPMS showed greater interindividual microbial community dispersion than RRMS in the full cohort, with a similar direction and magnitude but attenuated statistical significance in the age-overlap sensitivity analysis. Exploratory taxonomic signals were not confirmed by FDR-controlled analyses. No robust phenotype-specific differences in predicted SCFA-related pathways or associations of taxonomic or functional features with disability or circulating biomarkers were identified. Greater microbial community dispersion in SPMS was observed in the full cohort, but this finding was attenuated in the age-overlap sensitivity analysis and should be considered preliminary. Overall, these findings do not support a distinct SPMS-associated gut microbiome signature, although potential phenotype-related differences cannot be excluded.

title: Baclofen for Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: A Comprehensive Narrative Review.
abstract: Baclofen, a GABA-B receptor agonist developed as an anticonvulsant in the 1960s and repurposed for spasticity in the 1970s, is recommended as a first-line oral treatment for spasticity in multiple sclerosis (MS) by UK NICE guidance and is used similarly, though not necessarily designated identically, in many other jurisdictions. It acts at two sites within the spinal stretch reflex arc: presynaptically on Ia afferent terminals in the dorsal horn, where it reduces excitatory neurotransmitter release, and postsynaptically on ventral horn interneurons and α-motoneurons, where it hyperpolarises the cell and suppresses firing. Only a small fraction of an oral dose crosses the blood-CNS barrier, so oral dosing requires high systemic doses that cause sedation, ataxia and CNS depression. Intrathecal delivery bypasses the barrier, allowing a much lower dose and fewer brain-mediated side effects. Other drawbacks include a short, variable half-life, GABA-B receptor downregulation contributing to adverse effects and intrathecal tolerance, and withdrawal that has proved fatal. The narrow efficacy-to-side-effect margin is probably intrinsic to GABA-B receptor activation. This narrative review covers baclofen's neuroanatomy, pharmacokinetics, administration routes, efficacy, comparators, long-term outcomes, interactions, special populations, and regulatory history. Long-term follow-up shows durable control without worsening sedation, but the one study using validated quality-of-life measures found no significant improvement despite clear spasticity reduction. Weighing benefit against harm, this review concludes that baclofen offers a net benefit, but conditionally: only for carefully selected, individually titrated, and actively monitored patients. Because this is a narrative rather than systematic review, source selection was not governed by a prespecified protocol, some clinical estimates rely on secondary or aggregate data, and the underlying literature is heterogeneous in design and quality.

title: A Comparative Review and Benchmarking Evaluation of Step Detection Methods for Longitudinal Gait Assessment.
abstract: Gait analysis based on inertial measurement units (IMUs) enables scalable longitudinal gait assessment, with step detection as a foundational component. However, an understanding of available step detection methods and their comparative performance across sensor placements, clinical populations, and real-world environments remains limited. This paper addresses this gap through a twofold contribution. First, a structured taxonomic review organises the landscape into six families-rule-based heuristics, phase portrait, template matching, time-frequency analysis, adaptive oscillators, and machine learning-characterising the trade-offs of each in terms of noise robustness, generalisability, and computational efficiency. Second, nine algorithms drawn from five of these families, all but phase portrait, are benchmarked across three large datasets encompassing healthy adults and people with mobility-impairing conditions such as Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis, at multiple sensor placements under both controlled laboratory and free-living conditions. Accuracy depended on sensor placement, gait pathology and recording environment: step detection proved reliable in structured laboratory settings across most sensor locations and clinical cohorts, whereas unsupervised free-living monitoring produced a substantial degradation for most algorithms. Over all conditions, the three evaluated time-frequency methods obtained the best average ranks for detection accuracy, step-duration error and cadence error.

title: True Versus Sham Thread Embedding Acupuncture for Spasticity-Related Symptoms and Disabilities in Multiple Sclerosis: Study Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
Deep Learning-Based Multiple Sclerosis Lesion Segmentation at 7 Tesla: Comparison of Single- and Multi-Contrast MRI Inputs.
abstract: Automated lesion segmentation can support rapid and reproducible quantitative assessment and long-term monitoring of multiple sclerosis. Ultra-high-field 7T MRI provides increased spatial resolution and lesion visibility but introduces challenges for automated analysis, including field inhomogeneity, susceptibility-related artifacts, and spatially varying image contrast. Although deep learning methods perform well at conventional field strengths, their application to 7T MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated nnUNet using FLAIR alone, MP2RAGE alone, and combined MP2RAGE+FLAIR. The dataset included 115 longitudinal 7T MRI scans from 57 patients with MS, with 20 scans from 11 independent patients reserved for testing. DeepMedic was included as a comparative architecture. On the test set, nnUNet achieved mean DSC values of 0.72, 0.71, and 0.66 for combined, MP2RAGE-only, and FLAIR-only inputs, respectively. No significant DSC differences were observed between nnUNet and DeepMedic. For both architectures, adding FLAIR to MP2RAGE did not show a statistically significant additional benefit in the present test cohort, whereas MP2RAGE-containing inputs significantly outperformed FLAIR-only input. The findings of the present study provide preliminary evidence suggesting that the observed voxel-level segmentation performance was primarily associated with the inclusion of MP2RAGE. However, lesion-level performance depended on lesion size, indicating further investigation of contrast-specific effects on small-lesion detection.

title: Hypertension in People with Multiple Sclerosis: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy, and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Hypertension is a major cardiovascular risk factor, but its epidemiology in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) remains unclear. Whether PwMS have a higher prevalence of hypertension than the general population, the potential pathways linking the two conditions, and the association between hypertension and MS-related outcomes remain incompletely understood. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the prevalence of hypertension in PwMS, examines potential immunological, autonomic, vascular, behavioral, and treatment-related pathways that may link MS and hypertension, and explores how MS disease-modifying therapies may influence blood pressure regulation. It also reviews evidence on the association between hypertension and neurological disability, mobility, cognitive function, visual outcomes, and markers of neurodegeneration in PwMS, as well as hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in women with MS. Finally, it discusses the clinical implications of these findings and identifies priorities for future research.

title: Effects of blood flow restriction therapy on lower-limb strength in multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease that impairs muscle strength, gait, and functional capacity. Blood flow restriction (BFR) therapy has emerged as a promising low-load rehabilitation strategy, although evidence in people with MS (pwMS) remains limited and heterogeneous. To analyze the current scientific evidence regarding the effects of BFR therapy on lower-limb muscle strength in pwMS. PRISMA-based review included a systematic search of eight electronic databases. Clinical and quasi-experimental studies involving people with MS that evaluated lower-limb BFR interventions were included, with lower-limb muscle strength as the primary outcome. The primary outcome for meta-analysis was de standardized mean differences (SMD) in strength. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PEDro, JBI scales, RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2 tools. Five studies met the inclusion criteria. Interventions ranged from 6 to 12 weeks with low training loads (30-40% of one-repetition maximum) and occlusion pressures ranging from 30% to 80% of arterial occlusion pressure. Compared with exercise alone, exercise combined with BFR significantly improved quadriceps (SMD=-0.55) and hamstring strength (SMD=-0.38), and possibly reduced fatigue (SMD=-0.35), with low heterogeneity across analyses. However, the statistical significance of the effect on quadriceps strength was lost in the sensitivity analysis. Methodological quality and overall risk of bias varied from moderate to good. BFR therapy may improve lower-limb strength (more consistently for hamstrings than quadriceps) and may reduce fatigue in people with MS compared with exercise alone, but the certainty of the evidence is low. The quadriceps effect was not robust to sensitivity analysis, and no clear benefit was found for sit-to-stand or gait outcomes. The evidence does not allow conclusions on equivalence to high-load training or on optimal occlusion pressure or intervention duration. Lager, high-quality randomized trials are needed.

title: Examining the effectiveness of theory-based nursing interventions for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS): A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this systematic review was to evaluate the effectiveness of theory-based nursing interventions for individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS). METHODS: A comprehensive search of the PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and Cochrane databases was performed to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between January 1, 2015, and May 1, 2025. Following a rigorous screening process in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, nine studies meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included in the review. RESULTS: The included studies evaluated interventions grounded in nursing theories, including Orem's Self-Care Model (n = 3), the Continuous Care Model (n = 3), Pender's Health Promotion Model (n = 1), the Theory of Goal Attainment (n = 1), and the Collaborative Care Model (n = 1). The findings indicate that the application of these theory-based nursing interventions were associated with statistically significant improvements across multiple outcomes, including quality of life, self-efficacy, activities of daily living, treatment adherence, hope, fatigue, stress regulation, lifestyle modification, and sleep quality. Most studies exhibited high methodological quality. CONCLUSION: Theory-based nursing interventions not only yield significant positive effects on physical, psychological, and behavioral outcomes among individuals with multiple sclerosis but also serve as an essential framework for guiding the planning and delivery of holistic nursing care.

title: A large, comprehensive labeled MRI dataset of the human lateral ventricle choroid plexus.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a highly vascularized structure located in the brain ventricles that plays important roles in multiple central nervous system functions. ChP enlargement has been implicated in many neuropsychiatric conditions such as multiple sclerosis, depression, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease. However, limitation in the accuracy of the current segmentation tools highlight the need for more reliable methods to quantify ChP volume in healthy and clinical human populations. The shape and size of the ChP vary drastically from person to person, and currently there are no large ChP datasets which allow comprehensive training of segmentation models. Here we introduce DataPlex, a collection of 700 structural MRI brain images where the lateral ventricle ChP has been manually labeled and checked by expert human raters. DataPlex is balanced and representative across a wide range of scanning parameters, demographics, and clinical profiles, and subject-level information will be available for each labeled image. DataPlex will be open source to support the creation of reliable segmentation tools for the human lateral ventricle ChP.

title: The implications of biotin supplementation on multiple sclerosis, hair loss conditions, and thyroid disorders.
abstract: Biotin, a water-soluble B-vitamin, is widely used as a dietary supplement for hair, skin, and nail health. High-dose biotin (≥ 300 mg/day) has also been studied as a treatment for progressive multiple sclerosis (MS), although the clinical benefit reported in an initial randomized trial was not confirmed in a larger phase 3 trial, and it is not an approved therapy for MS. However, increasing evidence suggests that biotin supplementation, even at over-the-counter doses of 5-20 mg/day, can interfere with thyroid function tests, leading to potential misdiagnoses of hyperthyroidism and autoimmune thyroid disease. This interference occurs in immunoassays reliant on streptavidin-biotin binding, causing falsely elevated free thyroid hormone levels (T3, T4) and falsely suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), with the extent of interference varying by assay and laboratory platform. In this narrative review of clinical studies and case reports, we found that patients with MS and hair loss pathology, such as alopecia areata (AA), conditions frequently coexisting with thyroid dysfunction, may be vulnerable to misinterpretation of thyroid lab results due to biotin supplementation. Several case reports illustrate patients with MS misdiagnosed with Graves' disease or hyperthyroidism while taking high-dose biotin, with laboratory values normalizing after temporary discontinuation. In AA, no such cases have been reported to date; however, over 40% of AA patients exhibit thyroid autoantibodies and many patients with hair loss use biotin, suggesting a potential, though not yet demonstrated, risk in this population. Given the increasing use of biotin, clinicians must be aware of its impact on laboratory assays and ask patients about biotin use before thyroid function testing. The discontinuation period needed to avoid interference is not uniform and depends on the dose, renal function, and assay used; 24-72 hours is often sufficient for over-the-counter doses, whereas longer intervals may be needed for high-dose therapy. Improved awareness can prevent unnecessary treatments and misdiagnoses in individuals with MS, AA, and other autoimmune conditions. This review integrates neurological and dermatological autoimmune overlap in the context of biotin interference and addresses an underexplored gap in the literature. Further research is needed to examine biotin interference across different laboratory methodologies and patient populations.

title: Glial Contributions to Pain in Neurodegenerative Disease Models: A Systematic Review of Microglial and Astrocytic Evidence.
Bilateral Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia Caused by Minor Head Injury: A Case Report.
abstract: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) is rare, with vascular disease and multiple sclerosis being the most common causes. We report an unusual case of isolated bilateral INO following minor brain injury. A 61-year-old Asian woman developed binocular diplopia after a minor motorbike accident. Neurological examination revealed bilateral INO with impaired adduction in both eyes and abducting nystagmus in the contralateral eye. Initial brain computed tomography was unremarkable, but brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) 2 days later revealed a subtle paramedian pontomesencephalic hyperintensity on T2-weighted imaging, which became more pronounced with contrast enhancement, suggesting the axonal injury secondary to trauma. Minor head trauma can cause bilateral INO due to subtle brainstem injury, even without other deficits. Shear forces may lead to vascular and axonal damage in the medial longitudinal fasciculus. MRI with contrast is essential for detection. Although rare, isolated bilateral INO should be considered posthead trauma.

title: Congenital Hypoplasia of the C1 Posterior Arch Masquerading as Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report.
abstract: Hypoplasia of the C1 posterior arch is a rare congenital anomaly, classified using the Currarino system into subtypes A through E depending on the extent and nature of arch deficiency. The majority of cases are incidental radiological findings; symptomatic presentations causing cervical myelopathy are exceptionally uncommon and not well represented in the surgical literature. In such cases, the absence of established management guidelines renders clinical decision-making particularly challenging. We present a case of a 45-year-old male surgeon who presented with a one-year history of episodic bilateral upper and lower limb weakness. Initial investigations, including brain and cervical spine MRI, were interpreted as consistent with a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, for which treatment was commenced. Following a symptom-free interval after a one-month course of corticosteroids, the patient experienced a recurrence at eight months, prompting dynamic MRI of the cervical spine, which revealed a type C hypoplastic C1 posterior arch causing dynamic spinal cord compression during hyperextension. The diagnosis was revised accordingly. Supplementary investigations confirmed atlantoaxial stability and normal vertebral artery anatomy bilaterally. The patient provided consent and underwent posterior surgical decompression of the entire posterior arch, without instrumented fusion. Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring guided the extent of resection; decompression began on the fibrous left-sided arch, extending to the level of the vertebral artery groove, followed by the bony right-sided arch, sequenced to preserve facet joint integrity. The patient achieved complete symptom resolution postoperatively. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by symptomatic C1 arch hypoplasia, which may mimic demyelinating disease, and demonstrates that surgical decompression, guided by intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring and tailored to arch morphology, can achieve excellent neurological outcomes without the need for instrumented stabilisation.

title: Coding Pregnancy: How Classification May Shape Clinical Research and Practice.
journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
abstract: RATIONALE, AIMS, AND OBJECTIVES: The underrepresentation of pregnant people in clinical research limits the availability of reliable evidence for clinical practice. While this gap is often attributed to ethical and regulatory constraints, less attention has been paid to the role of medical classification systems in shaping the utility of Real-World Data (RWD). This paper examines how the coding of pregnancy within the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) and the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) may influence evidence generation and use. METHODS: We conducted a conceptual analysis of ICD and MedDRA, focusing on how pregnancy and related events are encoded. Drawing on literature from medical classification, pharmacovigilance, and evidence-based practice, we assess how classificatory fragmentation may affect data identification, retrieval and interpretation. An example from multiple sclerosis care is used for contextual illustration. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy-related information is fragmented across different coding elements, without explicitly capturing the crucial temporal and clinical context. This structural limitation may hinder the reconstruction of pregnancy episodes, affecting the capacity of observational research to compensate for interventional research gaps. To overcome this, we propose a three-step approach: (1) providing dedicated training on the correct use and interpretation of existing classification systems; (2) complementing these infrastructures with a standardised minimum dataset to systematically link pregnancy variables; and (3) establishing a feedback loop from secondary research to continuously improve clinical documentation. Ultimately, this strategy can support robust RWD generation and more inclusive, evidence-based care.

title: Establishing Potosi Virus as a Human Pathogen: Fatal Neuroinvasive Disease in a B-Cell-Depleted Patient.
abstract: To establish Potosi virus, a mosquito-borne member of the family Case report. A 37-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis on long-term rituximab developed rapidly progressive dementia. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive generalized atrophy. CSF showed transient, minimal lymphocytic pleocytosis. Extensive infectious, autoimmune, and prion evaluations were unrevealing, but CSF metagenomic sequencing detected all 3 genome segments for Potosi virus. Postmortem examination revealed diffuse meningoencephalitis with T-cell-predominant leptomeningeal and perivascular inflammation. Molecular analyses confirmed multiple nucleotide sequences with >99+% concordance with a known Potosi strain, with widespread viral infection confirmed by immunohistochemistry demonstrating intracellular and extracellular viral antigen. Electron microscopy demonstrated particles of a size consistent with the Potosi virus can cause fatal neuroinvasive disease in humans, as evidenced by convergent postmortem neuropathologic, molecular, and ultrastructural evidence. Chronic B-cell depletion may increase susceptibility to severe disease with arboviral infections, which may present without conventional CNS inflammatory markers. CSF metagenomic sequencing should be considered in immunocompromised patients with unexplained progressive neurologic decline.

title: Gray Matter Damage and Long-Term Disability, Cognitive Outcome, and Survival in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis.
Mesenchymal Stem Cell Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis: Harnessing Immunological Properties.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease triggered by damage to the central nervous system (CNS). This CNS damage is caused by the attack of autoreactive T cells against the myelin sheath. Genetic and environmental factors contribute to the development of MS, and the condition causes serious disabilities and exerts substantial health burdens. Although various disease-modifying agents have been developed, they have critical limitations; hence, effective interventions are required. In this context, cell transplantation therapy using mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), hematopoietic stem cells, neural precursors, neural stem cells, and induced pluripotent stem cells is considered a feasible alternative therapeutic approach. MSCs are adult stem cells that differentiate into multiple lineages and exert immunomodulatory, neuroprotective, and neuroregenerative effects. Therefore, MSCs are considered a promising treatment option for MS owing to their ease of isolation and low immunogenicity. This review summarizes the potential therapeutic benefits of the latest MSC-based approaches for MS treatment in animal models and humans. Furthermore, the review discusses the immunological role of MSCs and future directions for their applications.

title: Impact of the Family-Centered Empowerment Model on Health-Promoting Lifestyle and Psychological Well-Being in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease that can affect patients' health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being and may also place substantial demands on family caregivers. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a family-centered empowerment intervention based on the Family-Centered Empowerment Model (FCEM) on health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being among patients with MS, with the active involvement of their primary family caregivers. METHODS: This randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted from February to April 2025 at an MS clinic in Fars Province, southern Iran. It included 70 patient-caregiver dyads, comprising 70 patients with MS and their primary family caregivers. The dyads were randomly assigned to the intervention or control group, with 35 dyads in each group. Patients and caregivers in the intervention group took part in a structured family-centered empowerment program based on the four-stage FCEM. The program consisted of five to seven face-to-face educational sessions attended jointly by the patients and their primary family caregivers. The control group continued to receive routine care. Health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being were assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at the 2-month follow-up. RESULTS: At baseline, the two groups did not differ significantly in health-promoting lifestyle or psychological well-being (p > 0.05). Following the intervention, the mean health-promoting lifestyle score was 126.40 ± 25.18 in the intervention group and 102.62 ± 25.18 in the control group (p < 0.001). At the 2-month follow-up, the corresponding scores were 124.34 ± 22.39 and 104.22 ± 20.23, respectively (p < 0.001). A similar pattern was observed for psychological well-being. Immediately after the intervention, the mean score was 73.68 ± 13.83 in the intervention group, compared with 59.62 ± 10.24 in the control group (p < 0.001). At 2 months, the scores were 71.51 ± 12.82 and 61.34 ± 11.55, respectively (p < 0.001). Within the intervention group, scores increased significantly from baseline to both the post-intervention assessment and the 2-month follow-up (p < 0.001). Changes in the control group were comparatively small. CONCLUSION: A family-centered empowerment intervention based on the FCEM was associated with greater improvements in health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being among patients with MS compared with routine care. Involving primary family caregivers in MS education and self-management support may be a useful component of family-centered care. Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials: IRCT registration number: IRCT20190917044802N12. Registration date: 10/01/2025.

title: Neurodegenerative Diseases: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, Classification, Pathophysiology, Clinical Features, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are a growing cause of disability worldwide, particularly as populations age. Although these disorders differ in etiology and clinical presentation, advances in genetics, neuropathology, and biomarker research have identified shared disturbances in protein homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and immune regulation. These processes may contribute to selective neuronal vulnerability and neural circuit dysfunction. These findings are refining disease classification and diagnosis, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Disease-specific abnormalities remain essential to clinical interpretation and treatment selection. Existing reviews often focus on individual disorders or isolated mechanisms, leaving the links between shared biology and disease-specific phenotypes insufficiently clear. We synthesize evidence on the epidemiology, risk factors, classification, and pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, frontotemporal dementia, Friedreich's ataxia, and multiple sclerosis. We compare their clinical manifestations and diagnostic approaches, including the evolving role of biomarkers, and critically assess established and emerging therapies. By distinguishing shared mechanisms from disease-specific abnormalities, we identify key translational gaps and explore how common biological disturbances may lead to distinct clinical trajectories. This cross-disease perspective may inform diagnostic reasoning, treatment development, and future comparative research.

title: Metabolomic Profiles Associated With Disease Severity in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sensitive, minimally invasive biomarkers that reflect functional decline in multiple sclerosis (MS) are still lacking. Untargeted metabolomic profiling allows unbiased discovery of circulating biomarkers and dysregulated biological pathways underlying MS onset and progression. We aimed to identify candidate circulating metabolite signatures correlated with clinical, imaging, and patient-reported outcomes in MS and to characterize the underlying metabolic pathways. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of untargeted circulating metabolomic profiles from 541 samples of 323 people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), including both relapsing-remitting and progressive forms, detecting 332 metabolites. Associations between metabolite levels and outcomes, including clinical disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale), functional tests (walking speed, manual dexterity, and processing speed), Neuro-QoL patient-reported domains, optical coherence tomography-derived retinal layer thicknesses, and MRI-derived measures, were assessed using linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, race, treatment status, and MS subtype. To identify clusters of metabolites jointly linked to outcomes, we applied Hierarchical All-Against-All Association Analysis and weighted correlation network analysis. Pathway enrichment was also performed using Fast Gene Set Enrichment Analysis on ranked effect sizes based on the RaMP database, excluding pathways with fewer than 3 metabolites. RESULTS: We identified multiple metabolites consistently associated with MS severity across clinical, patient-reported, and imaging domains. Metabolites such as p-cresol sulfate, p-cresol glucuronide, phenylacetylglutamine, and carnitine-derived species were linked to greater disease severity, whereas tryptophan betaine, ergothioneine, N-acetylcarnosine, and indolepropionate were associated with more favorable outcomes. Pathway analyses highlighted amino acid transport and metabolism, aromatic and branched-chain amino acid pathways, and solute carrier transporter systems, as well as bile acid, sphingolipid, and carnitine-related pathways linked to MS severity. DISCUSSION: Comprehensive integration of metabolomic, clinical, and imaging data in PwMS highlights distinct metabolites and metabolic pathways associated with MS severity. These candidate metabolites warrant external validation in independent cohorts and provide a rationale for future biomarker discovery studies aimed at improving disease monitoring and management in MS.

title: Clear Positive MOG Antibodies in Adults With Multiple Sclerosis Features: Diagnostic Challenges.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Distinguishing multiple sclerosis (MS) from myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) can be challenging because of some shared clinical and radiologic features. We aimed to describe adults with clear positive serum MOG antibodies (MOG-Abs) presenting with MS features and rethink their nosological framework. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal study within the French NOMADMUS cohort and included adults from 2015 to 2025 tested clear positive for MOG-Ab in the serum with at least 1 MS-suggestive feature: (1) biological (CSF-specific oligoclonal bands [OCBs] and/or kappa free light chain index [KFLCi] ≥5.7) or (2) radiologic (≥1 lesion among juxtacortical lesion, Dawson finger, or inferior temporal lobe lesion). All MRI scans were reviewed blindly by an expert neuroradiologist. Minimum clinical and radiologic follow-up was 6 months. We classified patients as (1) typical MS when fulfilling 2024 McDonald criteria, with OCB and/or KFLCi ≥5.7 and showing no MOGAD supporting features, or (2) equivocal in all other situations. RESULTS: Among the 78 included patients (65% female, median age: 35 years), 23% were classified as typical MS and 77% as equivocal; all met MOGAD criteria, and 76% met 2024 McDonald criteria, without using central veinous sign or paramagnetic rim lesion, which have been rarely assessed. Myelitis followed by optic neuritis constituted the predominant clinical presentations in the whole cohort (45% and 32%, respectively) and in both groups. For typical MS cases, half of the patients did not receive maintenance therapy after the first MOG-Ab-positive event, 28% relapsed, 55% developed new silent lesions, and none showed lesion resolution (median follow-up: 1.9 years). For equivocal patients, 84% had OCB and 88% had ≥1 MOGAD supporting feature. After the first MOG-Ab-positive event, 72% initiated a maintenance therapy-mostly rituximab-15% relapsed, 46% developed silent new lesions, and 23% showed complete resolution of ≥1 lesion (median follow-up: 3 years). DISCUSSION: Clear positive MOG-Ab may occur in patients with genuine MS, and their presence may lead to therapeutic inertia. The substantial proportion of equivocal cases highlights current diagnostic limitations and underscores the need for longitudinal clinical and radiologic reassessment.

title: Long-Term Disease Control Following Completion of Cladribine Treatment in Multiple Sclerosis: Extended Follow-Up of the CladStop Cohort.
abstract: Long-term disease control after the standard two-year cladribine course in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains insufficiently characterized in real-world settings. We evaluated disease control, treatment re-initiation, and safety during extended follow-up of the multicenter CladStop cohort after treatment completion. We included 204 patients with relapsing MS who completed the approved two-year cladribine regimen and had ≥ 6 months of follow-up after treatment completion. Time zero ("CladStop") was defined as 24 months after first cladribine dosing. Co-primary endpoints were time to loss of no evidence of disease activity (NEDA-3) and annualized relapse rate (ARR) after CladStop. Kaplan-Meier analyses, multivariable Cox models, and mixed-effects Poisson regression were applied. Mean follow-up after CladStop was 44.2 ± 8.6 months. Overall, 81/204 patients (39.7%) lost NEDA-3. NEDA-3 survival was 82.8% (95% CI 77.8-88.2) at 12 months, 69.6% (95% CI 63.6-76.2) at 24 months, and 56.4% (95% CI 49.2-64.8) at 48 months. Forty-two patients (20.6%) relapsed, with an overall ARR of 0.06 (95% CI 0.04-0.08). Relapse rates decreased over time (rate ratio/year 0.74, 95% CI 0.55-0.999; p = 0.044). MRI activity occurred in 29.9% of patients and 6-month confirmed disability progression in 7.4%. A new DMT was initiated in 40.7% of patients. Relapses during treatment predicted earlier DMT initiation. Disease control remained durable in many patients after completion of cladribine treatment. However, over 40% initiated subsequent DMT during follow-up, indicating that prolonged treatment-free remission is not universal. Disease reactivation was driven mainly by inflammatory activity rather than disability worsening.

title: Safety of Multiple Sclerosis Treatments During Pregnancy: An Overview of the EU Regulatory Approach to Risk Management Planning.
abstract: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) may affect women of childbearing age. Information on safety of disease modifying treatment (DMT) in pregnancy is often limited at time of marketing authorisation. We summarised the EU regulatory experience with the implementation and performance of additional pharmacovigilance activities concerning safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding for medicines to treat MS. We reviewed EU risk management plans (RMPs) for centrally authorised MS DMTs to identify additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding. Information was analysed descriptively for type of measure, data collection method and data source. For non-interventional cohort studies and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases, information on current status, planned and actual size and duration was retrieved. We identified 17 DMTs that included 21 additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding across 15 RMPs. These comprised nine non-interventional cohort studies and four structured follow-up activities of pregnancy cases that had been started. Of those, three were terminated due to low recruitment with an inclusion rate slower than planned, while inclusion was faster than planned in three finalised activities. Inclusion rate was slowest in primary data collection and faster in secondary analyses and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases. Despite efforts to evaluate safety of MS medicines during pregnancy, recruitment and data collection remain challenging. Planning for use of multiple real-world data sources-including primary data collection, secondary use of electronic health records, and analyses of case reports-may help overcome these challenges and strengthen MS drug safety evaluations in pregnancy.

title: Digital Twins in Clinical Neurology: From Concept to Clinical Application in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Patient digital twins (DT) are emerging as a promising paradigm for personalised and predictive healthcare. In neurology, and particularly in multiple sclerosis (MS), the availability of longitudinal, multimodal data provides a strong foundation for developing patient-specific digital models, including simulation-based and mechanistic approaches. However, it remains unclear to what extent current approaches represent integrated, clinically embedded DT systems. We conducted a narrative review to synthesise current concepts, modelling approaches and translational challenges of DT in neurology, using MS as an illustrative use case. Existing approaches were mapped to core DT components, including data integration, predictive modelling, dynamic updating and clinical integration. Current DT-related approaches in MS demonstrate substantial progress across complementary development tracks, including multimodal data integration, predictive modelling, digital biomarkers, mechanistic simulations, virtual-patient frameworks and in silico trials. These capabilities represent important building blocks of DT development but have not yet been fully integrated into continuously operating clinical systems. Core DT functionalities, including continuous bidirectional data exchange, real-time model updating and closed-loop interaction with clinical workflows, remain limited. Key challenges include data fragmentation, limited interoperability, lack of standardised validation, and regulatory, ethical and economic constraints. MS represents a highly suitable model domain for DT development. Future progress will depend on further maturing and validating individual modelling and data-integration capabilities, as well as on their integration into continuously updating, clinically embedded systems. Robust validation, scalable infrastructures and appropriate governance frameworks will be essential to establish safe, effective and clinically actionable use in practice.

title: Correction to "Italian Delphi Consensus on Maternity Care in Multiple Sclerosis: Toward an Interdisciplinary Model of Care".
The Impact of Cladribine Tablets on Cognition Over One Year in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Preliminary Study.
abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), affecting >40% of patients. Cladribine tablets are a high-efficacy MS disease-modifying therapy to prevent relapses and limit disease progression. Our previous study showed cortical gray matter lesion stability over one year after the start of cladribine, though its effect on cognition is not well known. This study aimed to investigate the one-year impact of cladribine tablets on cognition in multiple sclerosis. Fourteen MS subjects [age (mean ± SD) 50.2 ± 10.8, 7.14% men, 57.1% relapsing-remitting MS (n = 8), 42.9% secondary progressive (n = 6), expanded disability status scale 4.1 ± 2.1] were administered the Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological Tests (BRB-N) and the Stroop Color and Word Test (Stroop) at an average of 1.5 months from cladribine start. The BRB-N measures information processing speed (Symbol Digit Modalities Test, Paced Auditory Serial Addition Test [PASAT]), verbal memory (Selective Reminding Test [SRT]), visual-spatial memory (10/36 Spatial Recall Test), and verbal fluency (Word List Generation). Stroop assesses processing speed and executive function. When available, alternate versions of the individual cognitive tests were used at follow-up to reduce practice effects. Paired t-tests compared within-subject baseline and follow-up data. After one year, no worsening was noted on any cognitive test. Furthermore, both PASAT 3-second total correct and SRT total delayed recall trended toward improved scores on-study, with an average 3.4 (p = 0.07) and 1.1 (p = 0.05) point increase, respectively. In this preliminary study, no clear decline in cognitive performance was detectable over one year in patients newly started on cladribine tablets.

title: The Emerging Role of Optogenetics in Multiple Sclerosis Research.
abstract: Optogenetics is a technique that uses light to manipulate genetically targeted neurons and has a potential role in the treatment of multiple sclerosis (MS). This review aims to examine how findings from current cell and animal studies in optogenetics may inform and advance future research in MS in humans. We conducted a narrative literature review of in vivo and in vitro animal studies investigating optogenetic applications in MS, focusing on their potential to enhance therapeutic outcomes. Our review generated 58 articles related to our topic, and 9 of them were included. Optogenetics enhances remyelination by promoting the differentiation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells into myelinating cells, thereby easing neural repair in demyelinated regions and restoring normal cognitive function in the animal model of MS. In addition, optogenetics offers valuable insights into MS by enabling the study of specific gene mutations, such as heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A1, paving the way for novel therapeutic strategies. This review discusses the future of optogenetics as a potential treatment for MS. This innovative technology may offer an improved approach to managing the disease, offering refined control over drug delivery, remyelination, and gene therapy. Further research should prioritize optimizing these technologies for clinical use and exploring their potential in combination therapies to improve patient outcomes. More research is also needed to reassess any complications or restrictions associated with optogenetics.

title: Lived Experiences of Bladder and Bowel Dysfunction for People With Multiple Sclerosis and Their Providers: A Qualitative Meta-Synthesis.
abstract: Bladder dysfunction and bowel dysfunction impact up to 80% of individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS). Beyond their physical effects, they can reduce quality of life and contribute to emotional distress for people with MS. Exploring the nuanced, lived experiences of people with MS who have bladder and/or bowel dysfunction is critical to better understanding these challenges. The purpose of this meta-synthesis was to answer the following research question: What are the lived experiences of bladder and bowel dysfunction for people with MS and their clinicians? This qualitative meta-synthesis included a comprehensive literature search of 3 databases. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were reviewed by 2 reviewers. Included articles were critically appraised, and reciprocal translation was used to synthesize novel, representative themes from the primary studies. Systematic searches yielded 3664 articles, of which 14 met the inclusion criteria. Three themes were identified: quality-of-life impacts, barriers to accessing health care (subthemes: clinician-driven access barriers, patient-driven access barriers, opportunities for facilitating access to bladder and/or bowel health care), and symptom management strategies. Findings highlight patient embarrassment surrounding bladder and bowel symptoms, limited clinician engagement, and low awareness of intervention options from both people with MS and their clinicians. More research is needed to improve educational interventions, increase access to specialized health care, and understand the perspectives of people with MS and bladder and bowel dysfunction in differing health care systems.

title: Examining the Relationship Between Perceived Social Satisfaction, Depression, and Anxiety for People With Multiple Sclerosis Participating in Group Treatment Modalities.
abstract: This study examined group therapy as a treatment modality for people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Specifically, social satisfaction, anxiety, and depression outcomes were explored in relation to treatment modalities. A retrospective cohort study was conducted to examine the relationship between social satisfaction, anxiety, and depression for people with MS in group vs individual therapy. Inclusion criteria were age of 18 years or older, MS diagnosis, and participation in 3 or more group (intervention) or individual (control) therapy sessions with an MS behavioral medicine clinician. Participants completed the Quality of Life in Neurological Disorders (Neuro-QOL), Patient Health Questionnaire 9-item, and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item scales. Demographic variables and disease characteristics were also examined in the context of treatment modalities and in relation to reported social satisfaction. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed. In covariate-adjusted models, baseline Neuro-QOL social satisfaction Anxiety and depression are negatively associated with social satisfaction, and treatment type is not associated with differing social satisfaction scores. Given this, patient-reported social satisfaction is an important consideration in the clinical treatment and interdisciplinary management of MS. Additional research is warranted to better understand outcomes relevant to different treatment modalities.

title: Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Triceps Surae Spasticity in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Spasticity represents a major symptom of people with multiple sclerosis (MS), frequently causing disability, pain, and abnormal postures. The aim of this study is the evaluation of safety and efficacy of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (RESWT) for triceps surae muscle spastic hypertonia in people with MS. Two centers recruited people 18 years or older with MS and triceps surae muscle hypertonia. People were excluded if they had other neurological conditions; had used anticoagulants; had intrathecal baclofen, botulinum toxin, and/or physiotherapy within the past 8 months; or had oral antispasmodics therapy modification in the past 4 weeks. The participants underwent triceps surae RESWT once a week for 4 weeks. Participants were scored on the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), the Numerical Rating Scale for spasticity (NRS-Sp), the Medical Research Council (MRC) scale, the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and the Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25-FW) test before RESWT (T0) and immediately after RESWT (T1). Self-perceived effect was evaluated via the Global Perceived Effect (GPE) at T1. Twenty-six people with MS were included (10 women and 16 men; mean age ± SD, 52.46 ± 8.39 years; mean Expanded Disability Status Scale score ± SD, 5.44 ± 1.34; mean disease duration ± SD, 14.88 ± 10.83 years), and 36 triceps surae were treated. MAS and NRS-Sp scores decreased at T1, whereas TUG, T25-FW, and MRC scores were comparable over time. Via the GPE, 73% of participants reported a self-perceived positive effect of RESWT on spasticity. RESWT may be efficacious and safe for treating spasticity in people with MS and does not adversely affect gait, strength, or dynamic balance. Further long-term studies are needed to evaluate the possibility of using RESWT as a treatment for spasticity in people with MS.

title: Exploring Factors and Nonpharmacological Interventions Associated With Respiratory Function in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Abstract. Multiple sclerosis (MS) can impair respiratory function due to demyelinating lesions that disrupt neural input to respiratory muscles. This dysfunction may result in muscular weakness, ineffective coughing, and respiratory failure. Early identification and management of respiratory dysfunction can improve long-term outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality. Factors contributing to early respiratory decline in MS are understudied. This review aims to characterize factors associated with and nonpharmacological interventions for respiratory dysfunction in people with MS. This review was registered with the Open Science Framework and conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus was conducted for articles published in English between 2014 and 2024. Eligible studies assessed respiratory function and evaluated nonpharmacological interventions or associated factors. Peer-reviewed observational and experimental studies were included. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened independently by 2 reviewers using Covidence. Findings from 11 observational studies identified factors that influence respiratory function, including disease-related, physical, and psychological factors. Nine studies investigated nonpharmacological interventions such as inspiratory/expiratory muscle training, Pilates, lung volume recruitment, and proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation; all showed improvements in respiratory outcomes. Although the impact of physiological, functional, psychological, and psychosocial factors has been studied in relation to respiratory dysfunction in MS, other increasingly common factors in MS, such as obesity, have not been studied and warrant further investigation. Nonpharmacological therapies show promise in improving respiratory function in people with MS, but larger trials with longer-duration interventions are needed to confirm the efficacy of these interventions.

title: A Positive Psychology Intervention for People With New Diagnoses of Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: The period surrounding the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) is physically and emotionally challenging. Positive psychology (PP) exercises (ie, systematic activities to cultivate well-being) have been shown to increase positive emotional responses, such as positive affect, and may aid in psychosocial adjustment to MS. Participants were randomly asigned 1:1 to a 5-week, at-home, self-directed PP intervention or a waitlist control condition. The PP intervention consisted of 5 previously tested PP exercises. Feasibility was defined as the proportion of participants who completed at least 4 of the 5 PP exercises. Acceptability was determined by participant ratings of ease and utility (0-10 scale) reported at the completion of each exercise. The effects of the PP intervention on a battery of patient-reported outcome measures were also examined using linear mixed-effects models. Thirty participants were enrolled in the study, and 70% met the a priori threshold for feasibility. Mean ease scores across the exercises ranged from 7.0 to 7.9 (scale of 0-10), and mean utility scores ranged from 7.0 to 8.1. There were statistically significant increases in positive affect (6.68; 95% CI, 2.58-10.78; A 5-week at-home self-directed PP intervention was feasible and acceptable to individuals with new diagnoses of MS. Larger trials with longer follow-up are needed to fully understand the benefits of PP training to improve adjustment to MS diagnosis, which may lead to better psychosocial and health outcomes.

title: Deciphering the mechanistic landscape of notch signaling in autoimmune pathogenesis.
abstract: Autoimmune diseases are a group of disorders with multiple etiologies that disrupt normal immunological function, leading to the immune system mistakenly attacking the body's own tissues. The Notch signaling pathway is a conserved pathway that is in part responsible for multiple cellular behaviors, including proliferation, differentiation, development, and death, through direct cell-to-cell communication. The expression and activation of Notch signaling pathway proteins are aberrantly regulated in autoimmune diseases in a manner that is closely related to their onset and development. We reviewed the functioning of the Notch signaling pathway in several autoimmune disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS), juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), multiple sclerosis (MS), autoimmune vasculitis, autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD), autoimmune kidney diseases and type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). We specifically sought to explore the involvement of the Notch signaling pathway in the occurrence and progression of RA to provide ideas and approaches for developing new therapeutic strategies for this autoimmune disease.

title: Pilot Study of Smartphone-Based Neuroperformance Tests in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: The Multiple Sclerosis Functional Composite and its iPad-based companion, the Multiple Sclerosis Performance Test (MSPT), as well as other traditional function tests must be performed during a clinic visit, which presents challenges for some people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Smartphone tests were developed, including a remote Timed Up and Go (rTUG), remote 5 Times Sit-to-Stand (r5STS), finger tapping test (FTT), and processing speed test (PST), in addition to open- and closed-eye balance measures. People with MS and a control group (CG) without MS performed smartphone tests and the previously validated, iPad-based MSPT. Convergent validity, sensitivity to disease status, and test-retest reliability were assessed. The CG (n = 23; mean age, 38.56 ± 18.5 years; 65% female; 74% White) and the MS group (n = 23; mean age, 58.5 ± 11.9 years; 48% female; 83% White; mean disease duration, 11.82 ± 6.72 years) completed tests at a single visit. Valid taps per second on FTT was moderately correlated with the manual dexterity test (Spearman correlation coefficients, ρ = -0.46 [right] and -0.41 [left]). Total number correct on smartphone-administered PST strongly correlated with iPad-administered PST (ρ = 0.78). rTUG had a strong correlation and r5STS had a moderate correlation with the Timed 25-Foot Walk test (ρ = 0.80 and 0.55, respectively). Ellipse volume and ellipse area, derived from open-eye balance tests, showed sensitivity to disease status (partial η2 = 0.08 and 0.07, respectively) and good test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.82 and 0.77, respectively). The FTT, PST, rTUG, and r5STS performed via smartphone application demonstrate convergent validity with their analogous MSPT tests. Open-eye balance outcomes also show promise for use in people with MS. These smartphone-based tests may allow for remote measurement of function for people with MS.

title: Outcomes of Comprehensive Multiple Sclerosis Care: A Pilot Comparison of Intensive, Integrated, and Usual Care Approaches.
abstract: A comprehensive personalized care approach may better support individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS) in managing their health, function, and quality of life than clinical care that does not incorporate evidence-based, comprehensive, and personalized care. This pilot study compared outcomes among people with MS who participated in a 4-day comprehensive MS care program, those treated in an MS institute, and those who received traditional MS care. This study was conducted at a nonprofit rehabilitation center. Participants were people with MS who (1) were in a 4-day comprehensive MS program (4Day; n = 24), (2) were receiving care in an MS institute (MSI; n = 10), or (3) were members of an online patient research platform (iConquerMS; iCMS; n = 21). Data were collected at baseline and 1, 6, 12, and 24 months via an electronic portal. They included scores on the Expanded Disability Status Scale, Patient-Determined Disease Steps, MS Impact Scale-29, Multiple Sclerosis Self-Management Scale-Revised, MS Walking Scale-12, Quality of Life in Neurological Disorders, and Spinal Cord Injury Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale. All groups showed improvements across most outcomes at 1 and 6 months. The 4Day and MSI groups had greater gains in self-management, self-efficacy, and quality of life, particularly at 1 month, compared with the iCMS group. Comprehensive MS care, whether delivered intensively over 4 days or through an integrated outpatient program, may enhance self-efficacy and quality of life more effectively than standard care alone. Further research is needed due to small sample sizes, pandemic-related challenges, and limited clinical data for one group.

title: Components of the Support Networks of Multiple Sclerosis Care Partners.
abstract: Care partners support many individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS), but little is known about the support they themselves rely on. This study sought to characterize the support networks used by MS care partners and to identify key characteristics associated with support network size. Fifteen MS care partners completed an online survey. Individual, semistructured interviews captured care partner support network content. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and correlation coefficients were used to characterize associations between network size and variables of interest. Participants were predominantly women (n = 13, 86.7%) with a mean age of 50.8 (SD = 11.8) years, and reported a median care-recipient Patient-Determined Disease Steps (PDDS) score of 5. Support networks contained a median of 12 different sources of support (range, 8-27). Friends and family members were the most common support sources, reported by 14 (93.3%) and 11 care partners (73.3%), respectively. Next were friends or family of care recipients (n = 9, 60.0%), and the care recipients themselves (n = 9, 60.0%). Only care partner resilience ( Natural supports (ie, friends, family members) were common and important components of care partner support networks. Care recipients were often important members of support networks, highlighting the dyadic disease experience. Findings emphasize the relationship between having support and maintaining resilience among MS care partners. Future efforts to implement novel sources of support must consider existing support networks and the characteristics of individual care partners that are most likely to ensure support uptake and efficacy.

title: Symptoms as Correlates of Health-Related Quality of Life in Black and White Individuals With Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Health-related quality of life (HRQOL) is a key health outcome and often compromised in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Yet the associations between symptoms and HRQOL across racial subgroups remain unclear. To that end, this cross-sectional, comparative study examined symptoms as correlates of HRQOL in Black and White individuals with MS. Black (n = 136) and White (n = 273) individuals with MS completed an online survey assessing walking impairment (12-Item Multiple Sclerosis Walking Scale [MSWS-12]), fatigue (Fatigue Severity Scale [FSS]); depression and anxiety (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale [HADS-A and HADSD]); and HRQOL (12-Item Short Form Survey Physical and Mental). Bivariate correlations and stepwise linear regression were performed to identify associations between symptoms and HRQOL. MSWS-12, FSS, and HADS-D were significantly associated with physical HRQOL, and HADS-A, HADS-D, and FSS were significantly associated with mental HRQOL within both groups: Black ( Our findings highlight symptoms, including walking impairment, fatigue, anxiety, and depression, as correlates of HRQOL among Black and White individuals with MS and may inform intervention development that targets the symptoms to improve HRQOL across racial groups.

title: Arterial Stiffness Is Higher in People With Multiple Sclerosis Than in Control Group.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, immune-mediated, neurodegenerative disease of the central nervous system with prevalent vascular comorbidities and associated vascular dysfunction involving arterial stiffness. This study examined the difference in arterial stiffness between people with MS and controls and whether the difference was accounted for by anxiety, depression, and walking endurance, variables not usually included in other studies of arterial stiffness in MS. The sample included 129 people with MS (age, 48.5 [10.8] years; 70.5% female; Expanded Disability Status Scale score median, 4) and 51 controls without MS (age, 48.7 [11.3] years; 78.4% female) who completed arterial stiffness, anxiety, and depression assessments and the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT). There were significant differences between groups in arterial stiffness ( Our results indicate that people with MS have higher levels of arterial stiffness compared with controls, but this difference is not explained by age, BMI, MAP, anxiety, depression, or walking endurance.

title: Perspectives on End of Life and Medical Assistance in Dying From Saskatchewan People With Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Medical assistance in dying (MAID) is a legally available option in Canada. Bill C-14 determined initial eligibility requirements (eg, a patient having a reasonably foreseeable natural death), program safeguards, and a definition of who can assess and administer MAID. Subsequently, Bill C-7 removed the requirement that death must be reasonably foreseeable. Saskatchewan's multiple sclerosis (MS) prevalence rate is among the highest in the world, and some individuals with MS have already accessed MAID. This project explored the perceptions of end of life (EOL) in Saskatchewan, Canada. Using an interpretive description methodology, 22 interviews were conducted with individuals with MS and 5 with key informants for data triangulation. Demographic and symptom severity contextual data, field notes, and reflective interview content were also collected and triangulated. Inductive reflexive thematic analysis was completed.
